#5252. Why Is Crypto Crashing Today? Bitcoin Falls Below $73K as Zcash (ZEC) Leads Crypto Losses

Why is crypto crashing? A hot CPI report raised Fed hike bets. ZEC fell below $1,000, the worst of 20 large coins this week.

Why is crypto crashing on Wednesday, November 11? The sell-off that began with Tuesday’s hotter-than-expected U.S. inflation report has carried into today, and almost every major coin is lower.

Bitcoin (BTC) dropped below $73,000 on Tuesday, touching $72,727 on Binance, and now trades at about $73,800. Ether (ETH) briefly slipped to $2,006, while XRP and Solana (SOL) are down 2% to 3% in 24 hours. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, a daily gauge of market mood from 0 to 100, has fallen to 29.

The report changed what traders expect from the Federal Reserve. Bond yields jumped, and bets on a larger December rate hike nearly tripled within two hours.

One coin is falling much harder than the rest. Zcash (ZEC) is a cryptocurrency launched in 2016 that lets users hide the sender, the receiver and the amount of a payment. It dropped below $1,000 on Wednesday for the first time since September 5. ZEC now trades at about $966, down 15.4% in 24 hours and 24.8% in a week.

ZEC has been one of this year’s best performers. It rose from about $526 on January 1 to a closing high of $1,653 on September 26. We checked the 20 largest coins on Binance, and ZEC fell the most over both the day and the week, even though it is still up 89% in 2026.

Trader 0x8742 opened a 10x long on 18,000 $ZEC ($17.63M) and is now down over $2.8M.

Liquidation price: $895.46.https://t.co/azzt3xvmay pic.twitter.com/wczndt7doC

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 11, 2026

So why are the markets spooked, and why is ZEC taking the hardest hit?

Inflation came in hot. The consumer price index (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% economists expected. Core prices, which leave out food and energy, rose 0.3% against a 0.2% forecast.

That reading crossed a line the Fed had drawn. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech hours before the report that core inflation of about 0.3% would make a half-point hike in December worth considering.

Traders took him at his word. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 0.5 percentage point or more in December went from 4.4% just before the report to 12.8% two hours later. They sit at 9.4% now, while a standard quarter-point hike is priced at 85.5%.

Higher rates hurt crypto in a simple way. They make cash and bonds pay more, so money flows out of riskier bets. On Tuesday, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield rose from 4.86% to 4.98%.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best Low-Cap Crypto

ZEC had the most to give back. We compared the price changes of 20 large coins on Binance over the past week and since January 1.

When markets get nervous, traders tend to sell what has made them the most money. ZEC has fallen 41% from its September 26 closing high of $1,653.

Borrowed money made the drop faster. On Hyperliquid, ZEC fell from $1,199.20 to $965.79 in less than a day. Lookonchain counted 32 traders holding more than $1 million each in leveraged bets on a rising ZEC price. Of those, 27 are now losing money, with about $23.7 million in paper losses between them.

Sharp drops have not always lasted. Since January 2025, ZEC has fallen 12% or more in a single day 14 times on Binance. Seven days later, it was higher eight times, with a median gain of 6.5%.

EXPLORE: Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

ZEC trades at about $966. It touched $961.07 on Wednesday, its lowest price since September 4.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, ZEC has fallen below its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $1,200.68. It is still above its 200-day EMA at $872.23.

For Bitcoin, the line to watch is Tuesday’s low of $72,727. Below that, $68,902, the August 20 low, is the next support.

So, why is crypto crashing? A hot inflation report raised the odds of a bigger Fed hike, and ZEC’s leveraged bulls are paying the most for it. A daily close back above $1,050 would be the first sign the selling is easing.

#5249. Solana (SOL) to Connect With Wall Street’s $4.7 Quadrillion Clearing Giant

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) will connect its tokenization service to Solana (SOL) in the second half of 2027, the company said on Nov. 12.

The integration will allow "digital twins" of Russell 1000 stocks, major ETFs and U.S. Treasuries to be issued on the Solana blockchain. In December 2025, the SEC issued a no-action letter that allowed DTC to tokenize these assets.

In 2025, DTCC processed $4.7 quadrillion in securities transactions. Its depository, DTC, holds and services $114 trillion in assets from more than 150 countries.

The DTCC Tokenization Service (DTS) will let large market participants convert conventional securities into tokens, move them across the Solana network and redeem them.

"DTC-tokenized assets made available on Solana – and all blockchain networks integrated with the service – will retain the same investor protections, ownership rights and regulatory safeguards that apply to traditionally held securities," said Brian Steele, president of DTCC Clearing & Securities Services.

According to DTCC CEO Frank La Salla, the integration will also free up securities for use as collateral.

DTS went live on Oct. 28, 2026. At launch, it worked with Canton Network and a private ledger. DTCC said that it adds new networks at clients' request.

"DTCC is committed to providing an open and connected platform that provides our users with access to mature distributed ledger technology networks like Solana that have established performance, security and governance features," said Nadine Chakar, global head of DTCC Digital Assets.

Nick Ducoff, general manager for institutional at the Solana Foundation, also commented on the news. "Institutions choose Solana because it already runs real financial activity at scale," he said.

According to Ducoff, the integration "connects one of the most trusted names in post-trade infrastructure with a network built for always-on markets."

As of Nov. 12, distributed real-world assets (RWA) in the Solana ecosystem reached $5.13 billion across more than 1.02 million holders, according to RWA.xyz. Transfers over the past 30 days totaled $16.48 billion.

The stablecoin market cap on Solana stands at $13.85 billion, with monthly turnover of $387.41 billion.

#5245. Bank of America Warns of 50 bps Fed Hike in December: Is Bitcoin Heading for Another 2022-Style Drop?

Bank of America (BofA) says hot CPI puts a 50bps December Fed hike on the table. BTC fell a week later after 5 of the last 6 big hikes.

Bank of America said this week that the Federal Reserve could raise interest rates by half a percentage point in December. The warning came after Tuesday’s October inflation report ran hotter than expected for a third month in a row. In Bitcoin news, the coin trades at $73,888 on Binance, down 0.6% in 24 hours. It dropped to $72,727 on Tuesday after the report, its lowest price since August 20.

The bank still expects the Fed to raise rates by 0.25 percentage points, or 25 basis points (bps), at its December 8–9 meeting. But it says the case for a bigger move is growing, and it calls the Fed’s decision to hold rates in October a possible policy mistake.

Traders are starting to listen. On Polymarket, the odds of a hike of 50 bps or more in December rose from 0.6% on Monday to 11.4% on Wednesday.

BANK OF AMERICA WARNS FED COULD DELIVER 50BPS HIKE IN DECEMBER

Bank of America says October's hot CPI report virtually guarantees a December Fed rate hike — and opens the door to a larger 50bps move.

Headline CPI rose 0.4%, while core CPI climbed 0.3%, marking a third…

— *Walter Bloomberg (@DeItaone) November 11, 2026

The bank’s call rests on three months of hot data. Consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, and core prices, which leave out food and energy because they swing the most, rose 0.3%. Both beat forecasts, the third upside surprise in a row in the Bureau of Labor Statistics report.

Bank of America now estimates that core PCE inflation, the Fed’s preferred measure, is running at 3.3% a year. The Fed’s target is 2%. The bank says price rises are spreading from goods to services, with electronics, airfares and hotels leading the increases.

Its base case is still a 25 bps hike in December. The change is in the risks: a 50 bps move is now possible, and the bank sees a growing chance of another hike in January instead of March.

The bank is not alone. Fed Governor Christopher Waller said in a speech on Tuesday morning that he leans toward a 25 bps hike in December. If core inflation came in around 0.3% again, he said, a 50 bps hike “should be considered.” It did.

Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more. That tends to pull money out of risky assets like BTC, and a faster pace of hikes pulls harder.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

The size of the hike has mattered for BTC. We measured Bitcoin’s price on Binance from the 2 p.m. ET announcement of each Fed rate hike since 2022 to one week later. That covers 12 hikes: six of 50 bps or more and six of 25 bps.

After the six big hikes, BTC was lower a week later five times. The median move was a 6% drop. The worst came after the 50 bps hike in May 2022, when BTC fell 23% in a week.

After the six 25 bps hikes, the picture was milder. BTC was lower a week later four times, but the median move was a drop of just 0.6%.

The record comes with a caveat. All six big hikes happened in 2022, a bear market that also saw the collapses of Terra in May and FTX in November. Those crashes made the falls after the May and November hikes worse.

The most recent hike was a 25 bps move on September 16. BTC rose 11.3% in the week after it, as the uncertainty that had built up before the meeting cleared. That makes the size of December’s hike, more than the hike itself, the Bitcoin news to watch.

DISCOVER: Bitcoin CPI Reaction: 10 of 13 Cool Inflation Reports Triggered an Hourly Gain – Can Inflation Data Reverse the Downtrend?

BTC trades at $73,888, down 0.6% in 24 hours and 5.8% over the past week. It sits below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight, on the daily chart. The 50-day EMA stands at $78,897 and the 200-day EMA at $76,449.

For Bitcoin news, the next test is the Fed’s own message. Traders already expect a 25 bps hike. If more officials join Waller and Bank of America in backing 50 bps, BTC may have to defend $72,727 before the December 9 decision.

Hyperliquid pays for the buybacks in dollars, so the decentralized exchange is able to buy more HYPE with the same amount of money when the price of the token goes down.

Over the last day, the platform collected about $1.46 million in fees, slightly less than the amount it spent on the buyback. Besides, DeFiLlama data shows that Hyperliquid currently earns more in fees than Ethereum, Tron and Base.

The largest part of the burned tokens, 48.85 million HYPE, was bought back by the Assistance Fund. The fund automatically receives between 97% and 99% of the fees from perpetual and spot trading on Hyperliquid, and the rest of the fees go to the HLP liquidity pool and to the builders of individual markets.

The Assistance Fund buys HYPE on the open market and sends the tokens to the "0xfefe...fefe" address. It is a system address that does not have a private key. In December 2025, Hyperliquid validators formally recognized the tokens held at this address as burned.

In August 2026, Hyperliquid also introduced the AQAv2 upgrade. Under the upgrade, around 90% of the yield generated by the USDC reserves on the platform now goes to the Assistance Fund. Each of these transfers brings between $14 million and $16 million to the fund.

Besides the Assistance Fund, HYPE is also burned through network fees. Around 1.24 million HYPE has been burned through fees and slashing on HyperCore, the base layer of Hyperliquid. Another 376,060 HYPE has been burned as gas fees on HyperEVM, the smart contract layer of the network.

MSCI evaluates whether a company maintains substantial operating assets and applies five financial ratio tests. In case a company fails to meet at least four criteria,

MSCI indexes track public companies based on market cap and investment risks. Global mutual funds and ETFs use these benchmarks to build their portfolios.

#5241. Why Is XRP Bleeding More Than Bitcoin, Ether, and Solana in November Sell-Off? Analyst Cites 3 Brutal Reasons

While Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana have also come under bearish pressure during November’s broader crypto market sell-off, XRP is taking a particularly brutal beating, leaving investors wondering why the token is underperforming its biggest rivals. According to prominent analyst EGRAG Crypto, the weakness is no coincidence, pointing to three key factors that could explain XRP’s sharper decline and signal why the token may continue struggling as bearish sentiment grips the market.

Crypto analyst EGRAG Crypto has highlighted XRP’s worsening performance against Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL) amid November’s broader cryptocurrency market drawdown. In a Nov. 10 post on X, the pundit noted the striking difference in losses since November 4, showing that Ripple’s XRP has suffered the steepest decline among the four major cryptocurrencies.

According to EGRAG Crypto’s figures, XRP has plunged 23.4% since November 4, significantly more than ETH’s 18.2% decline and SOL’s 17% drop. BTC has demonstrated greater resilience, losing just 10.4% over the same period.

The figures raise an important question: Why is XRP bleeding considerably more than its major competitors? EGRAG Crypto has pointed to three possible factors behind the token’s disproportionate weakness, offering a closer look at the selling pressure weighing on the Ripple-linked token.

The first factor is leveraged long liquidations, which EGRAG assigns a 30% probability. According to the analyst, forced liquidations of bullish positions, combined with weak buying demand, could be accelerating XRP’s fall. When leveraged traders are forced to close their positions during a downturn, the resulting selling pressure can trigger further losses and deepen an existing market correction.

The second possibility, which carries a 20% probability, is selling by early XRP holders. EGRAG suggests that longtime investors, often referred to as OGs, could be taking profits and rotating their capital into other cryptocurrencies. Such activity could increase selling pressure on XRP, particularly if large holders decide to reduce their exposure amid uncertain market conditions.

Finally, EGRAG assigns the highest probability, 50%, to what the expert describes as market manipulation or a deliberate liquidity hunt. Under this scenario, sharp price movements could be designed to trigger stop-loss orders and force weaker traders out of their positions before a potential recovery. The analyst believes this could explain why XRP is experiencing disproportionately heavy selling compared with other major cryptocurrencies.

Notably, these percentages represent EGRAG Crypto’s personal probability-based assessment rather than independently verified evidence of the causes behind XRP’s decline.

Beyond identifying the possible reasons behind XRP’s sharper decline, EGRAG Crypto has also highlighted several important price levels that could determine the token’s next move. The analyst identified the $1.00-$1.04 range as a critical stabilization zone, suggesting that holding this area could help XRP establish a floor amid the ongoing selling pressure.

On the upside, EGRAG believes bulls must first reclaim the $1.15 level before targeting $1.25. A recovery above these thresholds could signal improving buying momentum and offer some relief to investors after the recent losses.

Sharing a personal assessment, EGRAG Crypto said the ongoing price action appears more consistent with market manipulation designed to frighten newer investors into selling. However, the analyst raised a bigger question about whale activity, questioning whether deep-pocketed XRP holders are using the downturn to accumulate more tokens or adding to the selling pressure by offloading their holdings.

Ultimately, how whales respond to the current market weakness could offer important clues about XRP’s next direction. If large holders are absorbing the available supply, the sell-off could eventually lose momentum. Conversely, continued whale selling could make an already difficult recovery even harder for the sixth-largest cryptocurrency.

Yoshitaka Kitao, head of Japanese financial group SBI Holdings, answered "YES" when asked point-blank whether he still trusts XRP.

The question came from an X user. The user wrote that the past few weeks had been "truly exhausting" for XRP holders, and said that token holders feel that Ripple has left them behind.

Kitao answered in English. Most of his recent posts on X are in Japanese, and the rest of them are reposts of other accounts.

Kitao previously worked as an executive at Nomura Securities and later served as CFO of SoftBank. In 1999, he founded SoftBank Investment, which later became SBI Holdings. Today, SBI includes banks, brokerage, and insurance businesses, as well as crypto services.

The partnership began in 2016. SBI joined Ripple's Series B round and launched a joint venture with Ripple, SBI Ripple Asia. SBI owns about 60% of the venture, and Ripple owns the remaining 40%.

The same year, SBI Ripple Asia set up a consortium of Japanese banks to test Ripple's technology for payments, and the consortium later grew to more than 60 banks.

In 2018, SBI launched the interbank app MoneyTap. The same year, SBI's crypto exchange, now called SBI VC Trade, started operations with XRP trading. In 2019, Kitao joined Ripple's board of directors.

From 2020, SBI began handing the token out to shareholders as bonuses, and the payment service SBI Remit launched remittances using it with on-demand liquidity (ODL), including in the major Japan-Philippines corridor.

SBI kept working with Ripple during the SEC lawsuit against the company, which lasted from December 2020 until 2025.

Back on February 15, 2026, in rare long-form tweets in English, Kitao denied rumors that SBI holds $10 billion worth of XRP: "Not $10 billion in XRP, but around 9% of Ripple Labs. So our hidden asset could be much bigger." By his account, the combined valuation of Ripple Labs and its ecosystem is "enormous," and SBI owns more than 9% of all of it.

Kitao also talked about XRP at SBI's quarterly briefing on November 2, 2026. He said that investors buy Bitcoin mostly to hold it, and that the value of XRP depends on its use in payments and business ecosystems.

In August 2025, SBI VC Trade and Ripple agreed to bring the RLUSD stablecoin to Japan. In October 2025, SBI also invested $200 million in Evernorth, a company that holds XRP in its treasury. By now, SBI VC Trade has more than two million accounts.

Nvidia shares fell about 9% in after-hours trading on a new report about CEO Jensen Huang. Index provider MSCI also confirmed it will remove Strategy, the largest corporate Bitcoin holder, from its global indexes.

It trades at $73,588 on Binance on Thursday morning, down 0.4% in 24 hours and 5.8% in a week.

The funds are not helping. U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) lost $299.8 million on Wednesday, their fifth straight day of outflows. Nasdaq futures are down 0.9%.

Bitcoin ETFs Shed $300 Million, Ether Funds Lose $145 Million

According to SoSoValue, U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $300 million in net outflows on November 11, while Morgan Stanley's MSBT led individual fund inflows with $8.96 million. Spot Ethereum ETFs saw $145 million in… pic.twitter.com/5sn88B2JQX

— Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain) November 12, 2026

So what happened, and how much of the selling comes from the ETFs?

The first hit came from Nvidia, the world’s most valuable chipmaker. The New York Times reported on Wednesday evening that Huang had a second relationship with a senior employee who reports to him. The Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia’s board is preparing to remove him as CEO.

Nvidia had closed the day up 2.9% at $173.73. Within two hours, it traded at $157.99, down 9.1%. It is still down 8.6% before Thursday’s open. Nvidia has lost about 15% since last Friday. It first fell on Monday, after its board opened a separate probe into reports that Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

Bitcoin has traded closely with tech stocks this year, and it fell with them. Nasdaq 100 futures dropped 1.1% in the same two hours.

The second hit is closer to crypto. MSCI, whose indexes guide trillions of dollars in index funds, will delete Strategy from its global indexes after the market close on November 30. It ruled that Strategy looks more like an investment fund holding Bitcoin than an operating business. Japan’s Metaplanet and Upexi are also being removed.

Funds that track those indexes will have to sell their Strategy shares. JPMorgan earlier estimated that selling at about $2.8 billion. Strategy says the funds hold about 13 million shares, 3.1% of its stock. Its shares are down 1.8% before the open.

For Bitcoin news, that matters beyond one stock. Strategy is the steadiest corporate buyer of Bitcoin. Fewer index buyers for its shares could make it harder and more costly to raise money for new purchases.

The ETF selling started before either shock. To see how big the ETF side of this Bitcoin news is, we added up the daily net flows of the U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs for every trading day in November.

The Fed adds to the pressure. October’s hot inflation report on Tuesday pushed the odds of a December rate hike on Polymarket to about 97%. Higher rates make cash and bonds pay more, which tends to pull money out of funds like these.

#5229. Ripple's RLUSD Overtakes PayPal's PYUSD

Ripple's US dollar-backed stablecoin RLUSD has set a new record by surpassing PayPal USD (PYUSD) in market capitalization to cement its position as a top stablecoin globally.

Recent data from CoinGecko shows that RLUSD's market cap has grown to around $2.71 billion, enabling it to surpass its competitor, PayPal's stablecoin, with a market cap of around $2.69 billion.

This milestone was achieved less than two years after Ripple's formal introduction of RLUSD in December 2024, underscoring its rapid growth in the crypto market.

A prominent XRP Ledger validator, Vet, also commented on this development to underscore the increasing significance of RLUSD in the stablecoin industry.

"RLUSD is now a Top 5 USD backed stablecoin. On its way to be in Top 3," Vet commented.

Vet noted Ripple's long-standing contribution to building the XRP Ledger. He added that the increasing adoption of RLUSD could potentially lead to faster adoption of the blockchain by traditional financial institutions.

Vet stressed the increasing relevance of RLUSD's rising payment volume and increased use of the stablecoin on the XRP Ledger.

He also noted that RLUSD has opened the door to numerous integrations with banks and crypto exchanges.

The XRP Ledger validator further noted that these integrations could motivate financial institutions to not only run infrastructure to support the XRPL but also integrate other tokenized assets on it.

This new record for RLUSD comes on the back of several key institutional partnerships and exchange integrations for RLUSD that Ripple has been announcing recently.

On Oct. 28, Ripple announced a partnership with Coinbase to provide RLUSD for retail and institutional users across Coinbase Exchange, Coinbase Prime and its retail trading app.

As part of the partnership, Coinbase also announced support for RLUSD across different blockchain networks such as the XRP Ledger, Ethereum and Base.

On the other hand, Ripple's partnership with banking giant BNY, which is the custodian of reserves for RLUSD, is also deepening.

Besides this, Ripple has also managed to secure support from Standard Chartered, which launched institutional custody services for RLUSD on the XRP Ledger back in October.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

NEAR Protocol [NEAR] is in the news for all the good reasons. According to reports, the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem of NEAR is seeing increased activity through its cross-chain swap product, NEAR Intents, which has generated enough revenue to fund nearly $2.7 million worth of NEAR token buybacks in the Q4 of 2026.

Interestingly, this figure is already close to the $3.07 million spent on buybacks in Q3 2026, although half of Q4 is still left. So for those unaware, the buyback program began in February 2026. Since then, the protocol has purchased approximately $8 million worth of NEAR tokens.

In fact, so far now, NEAR Intents has collected approximately $8.68 million in fees since the 1st of October. Of this amount, around $2.82 million has been retained by the protocol, while the remaining $5.86 million has gone to solvers and partner applications.

According to Token Terminal data, revenue started around $315K in December 2025, climbed to a first peak of roughly $740K in February 2026, then fell sharply to around $200-240K between April and July, before rebuilding through the autumn to $650K in September. Finally, it crossed the $1 million mark in October.

This means that NEAR Intents is the main revenue driver, contributing roughly 74% of October’s total and the bulk of revenue in nearly every month, while the base protocol’s contribution stays relatively small and steady at around $30-260K.

That said, the platform recorded $3.76 billion in swap volume over the past 30 days, taking its cumulative volume since launch to approximately $37.3 billion. However, sustained buyback activity does not necessarily guarantee price appreciation.

The recent price action of NEAR trading at ​​$3.51 after a drop of 2.6% in the past 24 hours reflected the same. At the same time, the NEAR ETFs also saw outflows worth $5.74 million in the month of November so far.

Yet despite these weak market dynamics, the total value locked (TVL) in NEAR Intents’ confidential pools stood at $140.79 million at press time, up 402.7% over the last 90 days.

That said, the TVL started around $27 million in mid-August and grew steadily through early September, then surged sharply in mid-to-late September, peaking at roughly $185 million around 25-26 September.

After that peak, it pulled back and settled into a fairly stable range of about 135 million to 165 million through October and early November, with a minor dip near the end of October. In fact, according to a recent report by AMBCrypto, NEAR Intents recorded $10.41 billion in Q3 trading volume, up 66% quarter-on-quarter and 891% year-on-year.

This, however, coincided with North Korean hackers linked to the $6.3 billion Binance exploit using six memecoins created on NEAR to launder stolen cryptocurrency, moving approximately 117,000 NEAR worth $430,000.

#5226. XRP, ETH, DOGE: Tim Draper Predicts Bitcoin to Absorb Altcoins

Billionaire and longtime Bitcoin (BTC) supporter Tim Draper predicts a future where Bitcoin absorbs the innovations of other altcoins.

Draper's statement has major implications for big cryptocurrencies like XRP, Ethereum (ETH) and Dogecoin (DOGE), which have built their own ecosystems and now compete in the wider cryptocurrency market.

In a recent post on X, Draper compared Bitcoin's rising dominance to Microsoft's path to becoming the dominant software company, as the company absorbed successful innovations from other businesses.

"Microsoft never invented the spreadsheet, word processor, or slide deck. They absorbed them," stated Draper.

The billionaire investor brought up pioneering software like Lotus 1-2-3 and WordPerfect, which eventually saw their dominance give way to Microsoft's Excel and Word.

Draper predicts that this could apply to the cryptocurrency industry, as Bitcoin could become the ultimate absorber of innovations from alternative blockchain networks.

"Altcoins are the Lotus 1-2-3s and WordPerfects of this time," wrote Draper.

Smaller cryptocurrencies are thus essentially incubators for technological innovations that could eventually become part of the bigger Bitcoin ecosystem, according to Draper.

"They show that it works, then the innovation that pulls the strongest gets ported to the Bitcoin platform," he added.

Draper also supported his statement by citing the rising market share of Bitcoin in the overall cryptocurrency market.

The billionaire investor recalled observing how Bitcoin dominance rose from about 40% to 50% and then even further to 61%.

"Bitcoin is that platform," said Draper, claiming that the biggest cryptocurrency could follow a path similar to Microsoft's.

This statement has implications for the future of big altcoins like Ethereum, XRP and Dogecoin.

Ethereum is the leading smart contract and dApp platform, while XRP is mainly known for its cross-border payments and the wider XRP Ledger ecosystem. Meanwhile, Dogecoin is one of the most iconic meme coins in the cryptocurrency market.

Still, the growing ecosystem around Bitcoin, which adds more scaling and programmability through solutions such as the Lightning Network and projects like Stacks, shows how Bitcoin is trying to expand beyond its basic use case as a cryptocurrency.

#5225. Russia Legalizes Crypto Trading While XRP Stands Apart

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Russia Legalizes Crypto Trading While XRP Stands Apart

Platforms are able to conduct business operations in crypto, offering retail knowledge-based accessibility.

Russia’s crypto bid is going at a faster pace since the fourth largest economy around the globe introduced crypto trading for retail & businesses. The new set of rules, coming from the Central Bank Of Russia, limits regular investors to a 300,000 rubles yearly cap (roughly $3,600).

This allows buying & holding Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) & USDT through regulated intermediaries (brokers, trust managers & licensed exchanges). Everyone must pass a knowledge test plus review risk disclosures before starting trading activities, while XRP is considered an asset for advanced users only.

The Moscow Exchange already lists cash-settled perpetual futures (XRP/USDF) and related indices tracking XRP prices. These are available only to qualified investors, settle in rubles (no actual XRP is delivered), and form part of a broader set of crypto derivatives with substantial turnover among Futures traders across the scene.

Russian Central Bank: Exchanges May Conduct Crypto Trading from November 22, Subject to Prior Approval of Trading Rules According to TASS, the Bank of Russia said Russian exchanges may begin offering cryptocurrency trading from November 22, 2026, provided they first agree on… pic.twitter.com/txoYyq5vfL

The fresh legal framework dates back to August. Then, Russia’s President Vladimir Putin signed the inaugural comprehensive cryptocurrency law (Federal Law No. 282-FZ, “On Digital Currencies and Digital Rights”), setting September 1, 2026 activation window: contrastingly to the entry-level investor restrictions, qualified ones have no limits.

Meanwhile, businesses face hard limits, needing to meet a minimum equity requirement (15 million rubles, roughly $187,000) to run crypto services or custody services. The regulatory framework is way more lenient on businesses conducting cross-border sanctions to dodge the 21-chapter European Union sanction packages.

The retail crypto trading gets legalized on November 22, 2026, the related Duma documents state. The approved exchanges & crypto brokers are obliged to report the trading data and results to the central bank in accordance with existing reporting procedures for XRP & others.

For XRP traders in the region, the MOEX XRP Futures index allows up to 5x leverage.

RUSSIA MADE A MASSIVE $XRP MOVE!! pic.twitter.com/dmuUaPnsuP

Paying with XRP or any other popular crypto coin at a local store is still off the table. Goods & services are prohibited as a result of a separate ban, pushing crypto adoption in the perspective of an investment vehicle rather than a means of payment.

Still, setting up state-surveilled crypto brokers is a pretty big move that could inspire other major economies to do the same.

#5224. TSMC confirms data breach as hacker demands Bitcoin worth $215K — Details

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

2026 hasn’t been a great year as far as security is concerned. Whether it is Bitget or Binance, every single episode this year has simply highlighted how important it is.

It hasn’t been a great time for chipmakers around the world either. The latest news associated with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company or TSMC is a case in point.

TSMC is in the news today after hackers reportedly offered up private information linked to one of the company’s employees on an underground forum. According to the hacker, they have access to over 46,000 records right now. These records will be released publicly if the hackers aren’t paid 3 BTC or $214.7K within one week.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that the hacker in question isn’t exactly holding the information to ransom. At the time of writing, there hadn’t been any demands or efforts to blackmail. Instead, the hacker is looking for a buyer, any buyer, for the information in question.

For its part, TSMC acknowledged that “data of some current and former employees was disclosed without authorization.” However, the company was also quick to stress that there is no real evidence that any of its security systems were compromised. Its preliminary investigative report suggested that,

… this data matches the data in the system service of a certain cloud service provider.

TSMC also clarified that the data in question wasn’t associated or linked with any clients or production.

Right now, the popular chipmaker is working with cloud service providers and cybersecurity agencies to better understand what happened. It is also taking measures to make sure this doesn’t happen again.

Here, it is worth clarifying that the present case isn’t exactly a traditional ransomware attack. Instead, it’s a simple case of data breach since no malware was used and TSMC hasn’t been locked out of its system.

Still, this is an industry that isn’t exactly new to ransomware episodes. Back in 2023, for example, TSMC was targeted by the LockBit group who demanded $70M.

According to Black Kite’s ransomware report, for instance, there has been a 24% YoY increase in ransomware disclosures compared to the previous disclosure period. It also found,

The threat actor ecosystem grew right alongside the victim count, reaching 127 active groups by the close of the period and 146 by June 2026.

Finally, the report in question also revealed that the manufacturing sector accounted for around 22% of all ransomware attacks. Professional, scientific, and medical services accounted for another 18% of the total share. The ransomware breach that targeted DaVita Inc. back in 2025 and affected over 2.7M patients is perhaps the most famous example of the same.

The timing is interesting. Especially since news of this incident coincided with Nvidia hogging the headlines after CEO Jensen Huang resigned following an extramarital scandal. In fact, one can argue that the news has taken the spotlight off TSMC for now.

As expected, this has had a corresponding effect on the sector, related industries, and their performances. For instance, the likes of IREN, Core Scientific, and TeraWulf all fell on the charts in the hours following the aforementioned resignation.

Unfortunately, the market is brutal right now and clearly shows a serious level of pressure. A bounce from the longer-term average would be a good sign, but the confirmation of a market recovery would only come if we witness higher highs and sustained buying.

Meanwhile, the price has begun to follow a similar trend and has even fallen below the range of the previous zone of active buying, which was observed on August 18, 2026. It is now at 0.14, which coincides with the previous accumulation point as far back as May 2026.

The RSI trend is also bearish, and we may not see a recovery until a catalyst emerges in the broader market. Despite the RSI being in the oversold zone, there is no strong catalyst to help it rebound quickly, and the moving averages are also beginning to diverge.

This is an indication that the price will most likely continue to fall. Conversely, when the moving averages converge, we should expect a rise in volatility, which would be a more positive development for this asset than any other scenario.

Meanwhile, Chainlink's struggles in the market continue. The price has already broken below the 200-period moving average, and it's now in something of a free fall. LINK is trading at around $9.89, with the asset losing the $10 level as the decline continues.

The next support area in this scenario is around $8.20; below this, another potential support sits near $7. There are earlier trading ranges between the current price and those levels, so the path down isn't necessarily clear. However, a drop towards the lower level would essentially invalidate all of the gains LINK has seen since June.

Overall, the situation isn't much different from that of other tokens. If we overlay the charts for Stellar, Chainlink, Ethereum and others, we'll get roughly the same picture: recovery attempts followed by renewed pressure.

The difference is that with LINK, we might see an additional spike in volatility that quickly weakens the possibility of a rapid rebound, as the moving averages are only just converging. Such a move would be especially damaging if sellers remain in control. When a downtrend is accelerating, the price drop can become critical.

Overall, positive factors for LINK are quite hard to find right now. Despite the fact that the RSI is already approaching the oversold zone, LINK could still find a way to drop even lower.

A recovery is unlikely until a catalyst emerges in the broader market, with higher highs and sustained buying needed to show that the asset is finally moving towards a proper recovery.

Although Cardano usually follows the rest of the cryptocurrency market, here we see a situation similar to the three other tokens we have already discussed. The asset has already broken a fairly strong support that formed around $0.20, and the next potential buying area is now under substantial pressure, being tested around $0.17.

Apart from that, Cardano has already dropped below the halfway point of the recovery from June to October. Despite the RSI already showing oversold conditions, we aren't seeing much room for a bounce here.

On the positive side, volume is clearly moving down and isn't adding strength to the downtrend, which is a substantial advantage. We should also keep in mind that without a bullish catalyst, we most likely won't see a quick recovery here.

There is even a slight increase in volume compared with the beginning of November, hinting at the possibility that bears still have enough strength to pull the price down. The moving averages could come together closer to the next support, which might become the basis for a faster price surge. However, this is not guaranteed at this point.

Overall, Cardano has been in a downtrend since 2025, so the local spikes we could see from July to October shouldn't be taken as a guaranteed sign that the asset is recovering. Even though the price previously broke above the 200-day moving average, that wasn't enough to keep the recovery going.

Cardano might eventually move above it again and go further, but that is not guaranteed either.

Terra Luna Classic’s community got used to the monthly burning ceremonies, but this time it’s postponed.

A few weeks after Binance’s $6.4 billion hack following an employee’s laptop breach, the largest digital asset exchange across the globe is resuming most of their regular services. However, the Terra Luna Classic (LUNC) community has missed the monthly LUNC burn, coming from 50% of fees garnered from Binance’s LUNC-related trading pairs.

Typically done on the first of the month, this time Binance’s LUNC burn didn’t arrive at all, chain records show. That’s the first break in a pattern running since March 2023, when Binance pledged to help restore the downtrodden Terra Luna Classic community’s hope in LUNC’s long-term restoration efforts via continuous token burns.

On-chain records show 50 batches of LUNC burns being carried out by Binance on an earlier note. The last one, which was on October 1, 2026, eliminated 335 million tokens, pushing the exchange’s cumulative Terra Luna Classic burn count towards 91 billion.

That’s roughly 19.6% of all LUNC burns to this date, a considerable contribution in the deflationary campaign.

Still no statement from @Binance regarding the monthly #LUNC burn.. Although we understand the massive hack, I feel as though a statement should at least be made to #LunaClassic investors. Is this a temporary pause or indefinite?.. pic.twitter.com/Od2yH1kFgn

Some LUNC community members are floating the main reason for the delay to be apparent changes in wallet security, but Binance confirmed no such action. Naturally, the internal wallet reshuffling can be a normal practice following the multi-billion dollar hack and the day-by-day withdrawal restoration efforts done with diligence.

Back in August, the community behind Terra Luna Classic revisited the proposal 12223 to raise the on-chain transaction tax to 1.5%. Of that, 1.2 percentage points go towards burning even more LUNC coins. Meanwhile, strong voices in the crypto community have been advocating for more exchanges beyond Binance to burn fixed-fee allocations.

KuCoin & OKX were among the ones named in negotiations. The game-tested altcoin still has a massively over-minted supply of 5.5 trillion tokens in circulation, a figure normally ascribed to meme coins.

$LUNC AND $USTC BURN UPDATE pic.twitter.com/hboLcOFNdN

However, the LUNC chain restoration efforts have torched nearly 500 billion out of the original pile, showcasing what years of strict coordination can do for an embattled community.

Aside from the 19% portion claimed by Binance, the on-chain transaction tax and direct LUNC community burns make up the rest of the historical total. Regardless, the biggest hurdle for a proper Terra Luna Classic (LUNC) restoration point remains the stagnant trading volume.

Since the hard fork in May 2022, the cumulative burn efforts crunched 6.7% of total supply so far.

Token burning is a considerable deflation measure for long-term holders to ensure the asset remains at relatively bearable market value.

#5219. XRP Ledger Announces Major Fix to Come December 3

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) will be delivering a major update on Dec. 3, which will address the occasional sluggishness the blockchain network has been experiencing in recent weeks.

As stated in a recent XRP Ledger Operations announcement, the network will be rolling out its new version 3.5.0, which will exclusively include technical improvements and bug fixes, such as a lasting fix for the relatively slow ledger closing times.

"XRPL version 3.5.0 will be on Dec 3. Just improvements/fixes, including a long-lasting fix for the occasional slow ledger close times," XRP Ledger Operations said.

The developers have informed users that the interim fixes to help improve the situation have already been working effectively.

"Interim fixes already helped improve close times, and we are watching the network very closely," it added.

This is a critical advancement in improving the reliability of the XRP Ledger, a network widely used to process cryptocurrency payments, tokenization, and stablecoin transactions.

The latest improvement to the XRPL comes after the blockchain network suffered technical issues in October, when some ledgers were closing much slower than usual.

The XRP Ledger usually closes new ledgers once every three to five seconds. This ensures that transaction confirmations happen fairly quickly.

However, intermittent sluggishness was seen on the network, as XRP Ledger Operations admitted on Oct. 21. The team later confirmed that its developers were already working on the issue.

Afterward, XRP Ledger Operations started sharing a recommended configuration update for xrpld software with network operators such as validators and other infrastructure providers.

The temporary fixes were helpful. On Oct. 22, XRP Ledger Operations shared that the occasional slower ledger closures were no longer happening, thanks to the new recommended configuration.

That said, the developers remain hard at work to deliver a software fix that will correct the issue once and for all, a long-term solution that would not rely solely on temporary changes.

That is why the December release is expected to finally bring that permanent fix.

In the meantime, Vet, one of the notable XRP Ledger validators, has already assured the community that the blockchain network is always being monitored as developers work on more improvements.

In a recent post on X, he stressed that a great amount of work has been put into network monitoring, information security and engineering.

Vet said that their engineers are always on call to address any possible incidents.

#5218. Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

The crypto market crash deepens as $1B+ in longs get liquidated. Bitcoin sits mid-range at $72,969; fear at 28 isn’t a bottom yet.

Bitcoin fell below $73,000 on Thursday, November 12, extending a week-long crypto market crash in which traders who bet on a rebound were forced out of their positions again and again.

Bitcoin touched $72,735 on Binance, a hair above Tuesday’s $72,727 low and its weakest price since August 20. It trades at $72,969, down 9.4% from the November 4 close.

BREAKING: $BTC just fell to its lowest level since August.

Over $210 million worth of longs liquidated in the past 24 hours.

The dumping continues… pic.twitter.com/R7NVGivFnD

— Crypto Rover (@cryptorover) November 12, 2026

The altcoins are doing worse. Over seven days, Ethereum has lost 16.4%, Solana 14.7% and XRP 21.3%. CoinGecko values the whole crypto market at $2.42 trillion on Thursday, and Bitcoin makes up 60.5% of it.

Leverage made every drop bigger. More than $1 billion of bets were liquidated on Monday alone, almost all of them longs, the positions that profit only if prices rise. Liquidation means the exchange closes a trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out, and those forced sales push the price down further.

So is this the flush that ends the crypto market slide, or is there more to come? The data has an answer, and it is not a comforting one.

The sell-off had no single cause. Four pieces of bad news landed one after another:

Each hit forced out more leveraged longs across the crypto market. Thursday’s slide continued the pattern on a smaller scale. We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours. Longs lost $27.6 million, against $12.3 million for shorts.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Slides Toward $73K as Nvidia Plunges 9% and MSCI Drops Saylor’s Strategy

Big liquidations usually clear out the crowd. This time, the crowd came back.

In plain terms, traders keep buying every dip with borrowed money. That leaves fuel for another round of forced selling if Bitcoin drops through the next support. Bottoms tend to come when funding turns negative and open interest falls hard, a sign that leveraged buyers have given up.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Next Crypto to Hit 1 Dollar

The Crypto Fear & Greed Index, which scores market mood from 0 (extreme fear) to 100 (extreme greed), reads 28 today. Fear is usually read as a buy signal. The history says it is not enough on its own.

We checked every day since February 2018 when the index sat at 28 or lower, 943 days in all, and where Bitcoin stood later.

This year’s two bottoms came with real panic. When Bitcoin hit $60,000 on February 6, the index read 9. When it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1, it read 11. Today’s 28 is fear, but it is not capitulation, the moment sellers give up all at once.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, Bitcoin has spent 2026 in a wide range. The low is $57,800 from July 1 and the high is $87,396 from late September. The midpoint is $72,598, almost exactly where Bitcoin trades now.

The price lost its 50-week exponential moving average (EMA), an average that gives recent prices more weight, at $78,219. Its 200-week EMA sits at $69,597. Bitcoin closed below that line for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of the year’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

For the crypto market, three signs would say the bottom is close: the fear index dropping toward the teens, funding turning negative, and open interest falling as longs give up. None has shown up yet. Until they do, the 200-week EMA at $69,597 is the line that separates a pullback inside the 2026 range from a retest of the summer lows.

#5217. Everyone’s selling XRP right now, but why?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

XRP [XRP] has been sliding on the charts for weeks, and it looks like everyone’s selling their stash right now.

Whales have been steady though. They’ve been trading big, but we don’t quite know whose side they’re on.

Cryptoquant’s Futures Taker CVD has been sell-dominant since late August. That hasn’t changed yet so, two and a half months straight.

The only time this year Futures traders leaned buy-heavy was in the beginning of 2026. In that time, XRP has gone from $1.55 in late September to $1.05 now.

Spot traders used to turn a blind eye, but not anymore. For the most part, their CVD was neutral this year. There were some buy-heavy stretches in January, February and May.

That changed in October. Now, the Spot Take CVD is also sell-dominant. This is the first time that’s happened all year!

That matters more than you think. Futures selling might just be traders betting short. When Spot starts selling too, that would mean that people holding actual XRP may be getting out.

Usually, when people trade a coin this much, it’s because the price is rising. With XRP though, that’s not been the case.

Futures volume bubble map went red in late August. Through most of September and early October, it was marked as “overheating.” While that’s slowed down a bit since, it’s still been a fair spike.

It moved into “heating” in early September, was “overheating” in the middle of the month, and has stayed hot ever since.

Now, put that next to when Spot volume was “cooling” at $1.40.

Both markets are busy right now, but since it’s all during a dip, it may be indicative of selling.

Finally, CryptoQuant’s Average Order Size has shown “big whale orders” on Futures and Spot since early October.

That’s happened before as well. Whale-sized orders were all the rage through June, July, and most of August. All this, while XRP went between $1 and $1.25.

Towards the end of August, the price went back to $1.50 on the charts.

As with many others, this metric also only shows how big orders are, and not which way they’re going. Whales could be buying the dip, or walking away.

Either way, they’re the ones moving the most money right now. Whatever they decide at $1 is probably where XRP goes next.

#5216. Satoshi-Era Bitcoin Address From 2010 Suddenly Activates With $3.4 Million

A Bitcoin (BTC) address from 2010 has become active after being dormant for over 16 years. The address has transferred around $3.4 million in BTC.

According to blockchain tracking platform Whale Alert, the address held 50 BTC, which was roughly equivalent to $3,442,939 at the time of activation.

The dormant address had been inactive for 16.2 years. Back in BTC's early days, all 50 BTC were worth just $3.

Notably, this wasn’t the only old Bitcoin address that suddenly became active.

According to Whale Alert, another dormant Bitcoin address holding 50 BTC worth roughly $3,442,129 became active after 16.2 years.

The two transfers took place within minutes of each other on Nov. 13. Hence, the total value of the newly activated Bitcoin comes to around $6.89 million.

There’s no confirmation about who owned these wallets. Also, it’s not confirmed if the same individual or entity owns these addresses.

The reason these addresses are significant is that they date back to 2010, which is considered to be the Satoshi era.

In simple terms, the Satoshi era refers to the first few years of Bitcoin, mainly 2009 and 2010. During those years, the pseudonymous founder of Bitcoin, Satoshi Nakamoto, was pretty active in the network's development.

To be precise, Bitcoin came into existence in January 2009. It initially carried a block reward of 50 BTC. This block reward of 50 BTC continued until Bitcoin had its first halving in November 2012.

This is why these newly activated addresses’ holdings of 50 BTC match the rewards miners could receive during the early days of Bitcoin.

These old addresses always raise a lot of interest as Bitcoin had relatively few miners and users during those times.

However, this does not mean that these wallets are owned by the mysterious founder of Bitcoin.

This recent activation comes after a series of interesting activations in the crypto world. These are long-dormant crypto addresses that have become active over the past month.

On Oct. 22, a Bitcoin address with 170 BTC worth roughly $14.38 million became active after being dormant for 13 years, as reported by Whale Alert.

Prior to this, on Oct. 20, a dormant address with 500 BTC worth around $41.54 million became active after 10.7 years. In 2016, these holdings were worth just $194,955.

Later, crypto analytics platform Arkham linked the 500 BTC transaction to addresses belonging to convicted Irish drug dealer Clifton Collins. Previously, his crypto holdings were deemed inaccessible.

On Oct. 17, Whale Alert tracked activity involving old Bitcoin addresses holding 248 BTC and 167 BTC worth roughly $20.24 million and $13.65 million, respectively.

#5215. Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

Home » Regulations » Why Social Security Cuts Could Cost $500 a Month

A $10.8 trillion payroll tax gap is accelerating Social Security’s 2032 shortfall—and reshaping retirement and investment strategies.

For years, the impending Social Security funding crunch has been framed as a simple demographic math problem: Baby Boomers are retiring faster than younger workers can replace them.

While an aging population plays a role, a new economic analysis reveals a far bigger, largely overlooked culprit—a structural shift in how U.S. income is earned and taxed that has quietly starved the program of $10.8 trillion and shaved a quarter-century off its solvency timeline.

According to a November 2026 study from the AARP Public Policy Institute, the program’s trust funds could have paid 100% of scheduled benefits until 2059 if the share of the U.S. economy subject to payroll taxes had simply held steady at 1983 levels.

Instead, the retirement fund is projected to deplete its reserves in late 2032, putting millions of Americans on track for automatic Social Security cuts exceeding $500 a month.

Social Security relies on payroll taxes for roughly 91% of its annual funding, according to the 2026 Social Security Trustees Report. However, a shrinking slice of U.S. economic output comes from traditional wages covered by that tax.

AARP’s analysis found that wages subject to Social Security payroll taxes accounted for 41% of U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) in 1983. By 2025, that share had fallen to 34%. That 7% represents an estimated $10.8 trillion in lost tax revenue and interest between 1984 and 2034.

The report attributes this erosion to several modern economic shifts:

Under current projections from the Social Security Administration, the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance (OASI) trust fund, which pays retirement and survivor benefits, will run out of reserves in the fourth quarter of 2032.

If Congress were to merge it with the separate Disability Insurance trust fund, combined reserves would last until 2034.

Depletion does not mean Social Security payments will stop entirely, because active workers will continue paying payroll taxes into the system. However, without legislative action, incoming tax revenue will only cover 78% of scheduled retirement benefits in 2032 (or 83% on a combined basis in 2034).

That translates to an automatic 22% across-the-board cut in 2032—reducing the average retiree’s monthly check by more than $500 in over half of U.S. states.

With less than six years before the 2032 deadline, lawmakers face a narrow window to either broaden how the program captures revenue from a shifting economy or let an automatic benefit reduction take effect by default.

A 22% reduction in Social Security payouts would directly compress disposable income for tens of millions of U.S. households, reshaping consumer spending, personal savings rates, and long-term fiscal deficit projections.

First, concerns about the long-term future of Social Security could lead some younger Americans to take more responsibility for their own retirement savings. For some investors, that may mean looking beyond traditional retirement accounts to alternative assets, including Bitcoin and crypto ETFs.

Second, proposals to strengthen Social Security by taxing a broader range of income could have implications for financial markets. If lawmakers eventually target investment income or adjust capital gains taxes, the changes could affect investor behavior and market liquidity across both traditional and digital asset markets.

#5214. Here’s why Zcash could remove 50,000 ZEC from its grants treasury

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Zcash [ZEC] community is gearing up to vote on a proposal that could significantly change how ZEC funds its development and distributes newly created tokens. The plan involves removing 50,000 ZEC from the Zcash Community Grants (ZCG) treasury and redirecting its value toward future mining rewards.

That said, Zcash currently allocates 8% of newly issued ZEC to ZCG, which uses the funds to support developers, wallet providers, and other ecosystem projects.

These grants help maintain the infrastructure and software needed to use ZEC. However, rising ZEC prices has increased the value of ZCG’s existing treasury, which has raised concerns that the committee was accumulating more funds than necessary while continuing to receive new token allocations.

However, now, under the new proposal, approximately 55% of ZCG’s treasury (50,000 ZEC) would be removed from circulation within 30 days of activation. Going ahead, its value would be credited to the Network Sustainability Mechanism, introduced through the NU7 upgrade. This, in turn, would gradually return ZEC to the network through future mining rewards.

At the same time, the proposal would also end ZCG’s existing 8% allocation of newly created ZEC. Instead, this share would accumulate in a new Future Dev and Legal Defense Fund until the next halving takes place.

As this happens, the fund would remain inaccessible until a separate proposal establishes withdrawal rules. Lastly, ZCG would retain its remaining treasury to continue funding development, while the separate 12% Coinholder-Controlled Fund would remain unchanged.

For those unaware, the revised plan follows ZCG’s 3rd November decision to abandon an earlier proposal, which faced criticism for seeking to redirect approximately 98,000 ZEC from existing assets and future income toward mining rewards.

So, now, the next step is community voting, which is scheduled from 16th November to 30th November. Coinholders and community panels will assess the proposal’s support.

If it receives rough consensus, developers, and miners can work toward implementing it through a future network upgrade called NU7.1. However, there is no confirmed activation date yet.

This coincided with Zcash’s monthly active developer count having nearly doubled over the past two years.

According to Glassnode’s report, around 70% of its active developers have more than one year of experience in crypto development, compared with 58% across the wider industry.

Still, ZEC’s price action was under bearish pressure as it was trading at $986.40 at press time after a drop of 1.4% in the past 24 hours.

This followed a recent report by AMBCrypto wherein ZEC fell by 15.25% and Open Interest also declined 13.4%, indicating weakening speculative demand.

Ethereum’s [ETH] staking ratio has reportedly reached an all-time high (ATH)  of 36.3%, accounting for more than one-third of ETH’s total circulating supply. Well, the rising staking ratio suggests that an increasing number of ETH holders are choosing to lock up their tokens rather than sell or actively trade them.

This comes as Ethereum’s validator queues show that at press time, 911,938 ETH was waiting to be staked with a 16-day, 7-hour wait. Meanwhile, 264,211 ETH was queued to exit with a 5-day, 16-hour wait, plus a 7-day sweep delay.

Both queues are limited by the same churn rate of 256 per epoch, meaning only a fixed amount of ETH can join or leave each epoch, which is why a big backlog translates into longer waits.

In other words, more people want to stake than unstake right now, but the entry line is slowly shrinking, and exiting takes roughly 12-13 days in total once the sweep delay is included.

This comes as the total ETH staked rose from about 42.1 million ETH (roughly 34.5% of supply) in mid-August to about 44.5 million ETH (around 36.5%) at press time. Since late October the climb has resumed steadily.

Of this, BitMine earned $121.4 million from staking and validation activities, accounting for approximately 97% of its total revenue. By the 8th of November, the largest Ethereum DAT held 6.07 million ETH, of which 5.22 million ETH was staked.

On the other hand, SharpLink has accumulated 31,363 ETH in staking rewards as of 9th November. Its strategy also includes liquid staking through Lido, allowing it to receive wstETH in return for its deposited ETH.

All of this happened while the active validators moved in the opposite direction. As per charts, they held near 900K through mid-September, peaking around 912K. But again, they dropped sharply from mid-September to mid-October, falling to about 815K, and have since drifted down to roughly 807K, with a small additional drop on the last day or two.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Binance has published the final results of an unscheduled Proof of Reserves (PoR) report, two weeks after the cryptocurrency exchange lost $6.34 billion in an October hack.

According to Binance, the snapshot was taken on Nov. 12 at 00:00 UTC, and it shows that the exchange fully backs the balances of its clients. Shiba Inu (SHIB) is backed at 100.04%, and the other major assets on the exchange are fully covered as well.

The latest report comes after the Oct. 29 attack, during which hackers stole funds from Binance across ten blockchains in 20 minutes. Among the stolen funds were nearly 500 billion SHIB. After the attack, the exchange took an additional reserve snapshot at Bitcoin block height 975493.

Binance data shows that the net account balances of users stand at 50.67 trillion SHIB, and the exchange holds 50.69 trillion SHIB in its wallets. Of that amount, 50.68 trillion SHIB is held at the addresses of Binance itself, and the remaining 7.46 billion SHIB is held by third-party custodians.

Besides SHIB, the report also shows that the other major cryptocurrencies are fully backed. Compared with the previous check on Nov. 4, the BTC balances of users went up by 0.35% to 687,912 BTC, and the coverage ratio for Bitcoin stands at 100.05%. The ETH balances went up by 1.04% to 3.48 million ETH, and the BNB balances increased by 1.03% to 42.95 million BNB.

Still, the USDT balances of users went down by 3.68% to 24.3 billion USDT. At the same time, the stablecoin has the highest coverage ratio in the report at 104.34%.

Arkham Intelligence data shows that the known wallets of Binance currently hold 58.82 trillion SHIB. That is 5.88% of the total supply of the meme coin, and these tokens are worth $251.16 million. In this context, Binance wallets hold 8.13 trillion SHIB (about $34.7 million) more than the amount shown in the PoR report.

According to Binance, the PoR report only covers the deposits of clients and the coins that the exchange keeps to back them, so the company's own funds are not included in the report. Based on the Arkham data, Binance holds about 16% more SHIB than it owes to its clients.

According to Arkham, Binance is still the third-largest exchange by SHIB holdings. Only the burn address with 410.44 trillion SHIB (or 41.04% of supply), the U.S.-based exchange Coinbase with 74.53 trillion SHIB, and South Korea's Upbit with 64.14 trillion SHIB hold more of the meme coin. Robinhood, Crypto.com and Bithumb come after Binance with 57.12 trillion, 34.95 trillion and 16.74 trillion SHIB, respectively.

Finally, Binance said that the PoR system is still computing the final Merkle Root Hash using zk-SNARKs. After that, users will be able to log into their profiles and check that their balances are included in the overall ledger.

At press time, the price of SHIB stands at $0.00000426.

#5209. Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Drops Below $68K as Buyers Quietly Vanish

On-chain metrics show a massive 362,000 BTC demand gap opening up across major markets.

Bitcoin crashed below the key $70,000 support level on Friday, hitting a three-month low of $67,650 as a sudden leadership crisis at Nvidia, new MSCI index rules, and hot U.S. inflation rattled global markets.

Bitcoin fell 8.6% in 24 hours to $67,650 on early Friday, its lowest mark since August 19, extending a 10.2% weekly decline.

While yesterday’s pullback below $73,000 was driven largely by macroeconomic jitters, Friday’s breakdown reflects a rare convergence of tech-sector turmoil, institutional index risks, and evaporating spot liquidity.

Adding structural pressure to crypto equities, index provider MSCI’s November Index Review has placed Bitcoin treasury companies, including Michael Saylor’s Strategy (MSTR) and Tokyo-listed Metaplanet, at risk of losing their place in major stock market indexes.

Under MSCI’s updated eligibility rules companies that hold too much of their assets in investments rather than running an operating business could lose their eligibility for indexes such as the MSCI USA and MSCI World.

When a company is dropped from a major index, funds that track it often have to sell their shares, which can drive down demand and put pressure on the stock price.

Strategy’s shares dropped 6.49% in extended trading on Thursday. The company has previously warned that eventual removal from MSCI indexes could force passive funds to sell around $2.8 billion worth of its shares.

For Bitcoin, the bigger concern is that Strategy could slow its Bitcoin purchases if it becomes harder or more expensive to raise money. That would remove a major source of buying demand just as U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded five consecutive days of outflows totaling $1.43 billion, according to SoSoValue.

Market sentiment weakened further on November 12 after Nvidia announced that CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang was stepping down with immediate effect. CFO Colette Kress was named interim CEO.

Huang’s abrupt departure follows an internal board investigation and media reports detailing alleged extramarital affairs, including one with a alleged Chinese spy as well as relationships with Nvidia employees.

Nvidia shares fell as much as 4% on Thursday, extending a month-long decline that has wiped out 27.28% of the stock’s value. The Nvidia news added to pressure on risk assets, alongside declines in the Nasdaq Composite (-0.39%) and S&P 500 (-0.35%).

Rising inflation is adding pressure to both stock and crypto markets. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that consumer prices rose 0.4% in October, above the 0.3% forecast. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, also came in higher than expected at 0.3%, against a forecast of 0.2%.

The higher-than-expected figures have reduced hopes of near-term interest rate cuts and raised expectations of a rate hike.

According to CME Group’s FedWatch tool, markets are now pricing in an 88.5% chance of a 0.25-percentage-point rate increase in December. Higher interest rates could put further pressure on Bitcoin by making safer investments, such as U.S. Treasury bonds, more attractive

Blockchain data suggests Bitcoin lacked enough buying demand to defend the $70,000 level.

According to a CryptoQuant report, demand across spot and perpetual futures markets fell by 362,000 BTC over 30 days, with spot demand declining by 280,000 BTC and futures demand by 82,000 BTC.

Meanwhile, Bitcoin miner transfers to exchanges surged to 2,077 BTC on November 10, roughly 16 times the 30-day daily average of 127 BTC. About 97% of the transfers came from Antpool.

At the same time, stablecoin supply contracted by $14.2 billion over 30 days, pointing to declining liquidity across the crypto market.

According to CryptoQuant analysts, the broader picture remains cautious. Leverage is being unwound, but fresh spot buying has yet to return convincingly. Until demand strengthens, ETF flows turn positive and market liquidity stabilizes, Bitcoin’s recovery is likely to remain fragile, with further downside risks still in play.

In Bitcoin news on Friday, November 13, the BTC USD price fell as low as $67,568 on Binance as a wave of forced selling wiped out leveraged bets on a rebound. It was the cryptocurrency’s lowest price since August 19.

Bitcoin trades at $68,772, down 6.7% in 24 hours and 9.1% in a week. Ether lost 5.5% and Solana 3.4% on the day.

BREAKING: Bitcoin falls below $69,000 and ETH nears $1,900 as selling pressure accelerates in crypto.

Crypto markets have now lost -$150 billion in 48 hours. pic.twitter.com/29QW0khxOh

— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) November 13, 2026

Most of the damage came from liquidations, when an exchange closes a leveraged trade by force once the trader’s collateral runs out. CoinGlass data cited by several outlets put the 24-hour total at about $1.4 billion, close to 90% of it from longs, the bets that prices would rise. Those forced sales pushed Bitcoin through $70,000 in about two hours overnight.

The mood has flipped with it. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped from 28 to 20 on Friday, its first Extreme Fear reading since July.

In Bitcoin news this week, the question is no longer whether the market is scared. It is whether Extreme Fear means the bottom is close, and what the daily and weekly charts say.

The slide started on Thursday afternoon, when Nvidia announced that CEO Jensen Huang had resigned. It picked up speed after midnight UTC, when Bitcoin broke below the $72,727 low from Tuesday and kept falling.

We added up every forced closure in Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP and Dogecoin futures on OKX, one of the largest exchanges, over the past 24 hours.

Investors have also kept pulling money from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs, funds that buy and hold the coin itself, adding to the selling.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Price Crashes to $72,700 as Leveraged Traders Buy the Dip: Is the Bottom In?

On Thursday, we listed three signs that would point to a bottom: the fear index dropping toward the teens, the funding rate turning negative and open interest, the value of open futures bets, falling as longs give up. Overnight, two of them showed up.

One sign still points the other way. On OKX, 3.19 accounts are long for every one that is short, about the same as before the crash. Many traders are still buying the dip with leverage.

Market Intelligence: Crypto Analyst Predicts Best New Crypto to Hodl

Extreme Fear sounds like a buy signal. History says it usually comes early. We found every time since 2018 that the index first dropped to 20 or lower after at least a month without such a reading. There were 16, and we followed Bitcoin for 90 days after each.

The most recent case fits the pattern. Extreme Fear first appeared on June 3 at $64,014, and Bitcoin still fell another 8.5% before it bottomed at $57,800 on July 1. Then it rallied to $87,396 in September.

For anyone reading this Bitcoin news as a buy signal, Extreme Fear says the bottom is getting closer. It has rarely said the bottom is here. A move to the 2026 lows would match the median path.

On the daily chart, where each candle covers one day, Bitcoin sits far below both of its exponential moving averages (EMAs), averages that give recent prices more weight. The 50-day EMA is at $78,226 and the 200-day EMA at $76,325.

On the weekly chart, where each candle covers one week, the key level is the 200-week EMA at $69,555. Bitcoin trades just below it, and the week closes on Sunday.

That line matters. Bitcoin closed below the 200-week EMA for 16 weeks this year, in February and March and again from June to mid-August, and both of 2026’s bottoms formed during those stretches.

The overnight flush did part of the work a bottom needs: leverage came out and funding turned negative.

For traders following Bitcoin news, the Sunday weekly close against $69,555 is the next test. History says the final low often comes weeks after the first Extreme Fear reading.

#5206. Important Ethereum (ETH) Bug Might Be Finally Fixed

One of Ethereum's consensus clients has merged a fix for a validator pubkey cache poisoning attack, according to a pull request on GitHub. The patch addresses a vulnerability around the Gloas fork, which could result in some nodes rejecting valid signatures due to a bug in the global pubkey cache.

Gloas is the consensus layer part of the upcoming Glamsterdam upgrade.

The issue lies in a mechanism where the client stores validator public keys and their indexes in a global cache.

Technically, deposits that are already finalized should give the same validators on every chain, though it is a different story at the fork boundary.

The attacker needs 3 pending deposits just before the fork. The first one is a large top-up for an existing validator. The other two are new keys: A with builder credentials and B with regular validator credentials.

On the canonical chain, the top-up consumes the balance churn, so A and B are processed after the fork. A becomes a builder, and B takes the next validator index.

On the attacker's side chain, the topped-up validator gets slashed before the fork, and its deposit is skipped. This leads to A being processed earlier, essentially taking B's index.

The buggy cache assumed both chains would produce the same validators and imported A's key globally.

At the fork, affected nodes would reject all valid signatures from B on the canonical chain and fork off.

Realistically, the attack is somewhat complicated, as it needs a slashing at the right moment and a side chain, so it's unlikely to happen by accident.

According to the PR, the fix is to only add keys to the global pubkey cache once their activation eligibility epoch is finalized.

A new HeadPubkeys structure also combines keys from the head state and the global cache, so nodes don't miss keys if the chain finalizes without new blocks.

Whether other consensus clients had a similar issue is yet to be confirmed. In other words, the closer Glamsterdam gets, the more edge cases around the fork boundary developers have to catch.
