#5107. 35 Best Home Gym Equipment Items to Build Your Gym, Tested By Us

This gear will make you never want to leave your personal fitness sanctuary.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

WHETHER YOU'RE A weightlifter, CrossFit acolyte, cardio junkie, or yoga lover, a dependable home gym setup is a must. You might not have the square footage or budget to create a space that replicates your go-to health club or weight room space, but you can still achieve great workouts at home with the best home gym equipment.

Building your home fitness setup should prioritize space, functionality, and usability over trends. Choose gear that suits your needs and storage space. Whether it's a full-on garage gym or portable equipment, the best home gym equipment can help you make the most of your home workouts.

Read more: How Men's Health Thoroughly Tests and Reviews Fitness Products

From traditional heavy lifting (we love these barbell sets and weight benches) to HIIT workouts (this 15-minute interval workout is sure to make you sweat) to full-on indoor cardio rigs (like the best indoor rowing machines and the best ellipticals), we've tested and vetted something out there for every type of training imaginable. In fact, we've used hundreds of pieces of equipment throughout the years, from the most high-end, commercial-grade options all the way down to budget gear from Amazon. Our extensive testing process has involved a comprehensive evaluation of multiple factors, including durability, performance, suitability for different fitness levels, and value, to ensure that we recommend only the best.

SMRTFT’s Nüobell is the perfect ultra-durable adjustable dumbbell for my home workouts. It can easily be five pounds, perfect for warm-up work, or 80 pounds, enough to challenge most people on fundamental leg moves, Eric Sung, C.S.C.S., a member of the Men's Health Strength in Diversity initiative and trainer at Performance Lab in New York City, told us.

These adjustable dumbbells give you the convenience of 16 sets of dumbbells all in one compact footprint. They're easy to use and offer superior durability thanks to their machined steel weight plates. If you're starting a home gym from scratch or live in tight confines with little room to spare, consider these a must-have. Few items pack as much versatility and return on investment in such a small package.

PowerBlock is practically synonymous with adjustable dumbbells—and for good reason. The Pro 100 model is compact, rugged, and replaces an entire weight rack. With a range from 5 to 100 pounds, it offers more versatility than almost any other dumbbell on the market.

One of our testers, Maillard Howell, who tried PowerBlock’s Pro 50 model, said he liked how compact the dumbbells were and that the square shape lets you set them down without rolling away. Men’s Health Fitness Director Ebenezer Samuel, C.S.C.S., likes how easy they are to adjust. He’s also dropped these dumbbells from about four feet and reported zero breakage (though we wouldn’t suggest dropping them).

There’s not much to nitpick with these dumbbells. That said, they can feel awkward and obtrusive during specific exercises. For example, because your hand and wrist are inside the bell, they can feel clunky during dumbbell curls. Samuel says the weight distribution differs between PowerBlocks and traditional dumbbells, and he sticks with the latter for most accessory movements (biceps curls, skull crushers, lateral raises, etc.).

We dubbed this bench the “mid-range bench that delivers big value”. For around $350, we’re confident the AB-3000 is nicer than any bench you’ve used in a commercial gym and can serve most lifters for years. It offers flat, incline, and decline options, which most adjustable benches on the market don’t. You’ll never outlift the 1,000-pound weight capacity, and the redesigned 2.0 version features a longer back leg to eliminate side-to-side wobble.

“Hands down, my favorite feature is the ladder-style adjustment system—you can drag the bench to any upright angle in seconds,” says NASM-certified personal trainer and product tester Andrew Gutman.

There are a few trade-offs. The 2.1-inch pad gap, while common among adjustable benches, could bother some lifters if their hips land in the gap mid-set. The bench also can’t be stored upright, and at nearly five feet long, it claims a chunk of floor space. Lastly, while $350 is a fair price for this level of quality, it’s not exactly pocket change.

Read More: Our Review of the Rep Fitness AB-3000

Hammer Strength (by Life Fitness) outfits weight rooms for elite organizations—from the Tennessee Titans to Team USA Bobsled. And for good reason: When it comes to quality, dependability, and customization, Hammer Strength sets the gold standard. Even the Men’s Health weight room features Hammer Strength’s Elite iD Half Rack.

The HD NX rack is highly customizable. You can choose between two heights (86" or 91"), two storage depths (15" or 21"), and either four or six uprights. It's essentially a commercial-grade system adapted for home use. That is if your “home gym” resembles a college weight room. Before buying, measure your space carefully and consider your long-term training plans. Even in its slimmest configuration, the HD NX commands serious square footage.

But with that footprint comes unmatched functionality. You can outfit it with almost anything: multiple pull-up bar variations, band pegs, barbell storage, Nordic curl attachments, and more. The rack works with a wide range of accessories and is built to withstand hard workouts year after year.

The HD NX is the best rack money can buy, but you’ll need a lot of it. It’s overkill for most lifters, but for those building the ultimate home gym with no budget restrictions, this is the crown jewel. It’s a lifetime investment you’ll never regret.

Foldable squat racks are a game-changer for home gyms, and Titan’s T-3 Series rack offers one of the best values. When not in use, it folds flat to just five inches off the wall. Unfolded, it gives you the option of 21” or 41” of depth, with a substantial 1,100-pound weight capacity, more than enough for even serious lifters. It also comes with J-hooks (essential for racking your barbell) and a pull-up bar for added versatility.

This space-saver does come with trade-offs. Like most folding racks, it requires wall mounting, and the necessary hardware isn’t included. You’ll also want to make sure your wall can support both the 145-pound rack and the load you plan to lift. Even when mounted properly, a wall-mounted rack may feel less stable than a fully bolted-down or freestanding unit.

That said, for under $400 shipped (and with a one-year warranty), the T-3 delivers beyond its price point. It’s a no-frills, budget-friendly rack that doesn’t skimp on strength or functionality, ideal for anyone building a legit home gym in limited space.

This seven-foot Olympic barbell has been one of our favorite home barbells for years. The 15" sleeves are designed with snap clips to accommodate any 2-inch Olympic plates. It's built of 110,000 PSI tensile strength cold-rolled Japanese steel with a black oxide finish, so it's plenty durable. It's durable enough, in fact, to be rated to 1,000 pounds. That won't quite accommodate powerlifters, but it's more than enough for beginner to intermediate home lifters.

Most reviewers say it feels great in the hands (even without the knurled grip), though some report more bending than expected when lifting 350 pounds or more. But at roughly half the price of most premium alternatives, it's an incredible value, especially for any moderate weightlifters looking to upgrade their home gym without spending a small fortune.

REP Fitness' rubber bumper plates strike a strong balance of affordability and durability. Built with stainless steel inserts for easy loading and a stylish black high-density rubber, these plates are designed to take a beating, whether you’re deadlifting in the garage or doing Olympic lifts on a platform.

For those looking for a complete set, with color coding for different weights, REP Fitness also offers one with five different plates—10 lb (grey), 15 lb (black), 25 lb (green), 35 lb (yellow), and 45 lb (blue)—and for the cost of $775, you can get everything you need to get started. We recommend starting with four to six plates to get your home gym rolling, then adding more as needed.

For lifters who want solid performance without premium pricing, these REP Fitness plates offer great value on the market.

CAP Barbell's cast iron plates strike the right balance between affordability and durability. Built with a precision-machined 2-inch center hole for a secure fit on Olympic barbells. The plates feature a durable black baked enamel finish and are built to take a beating, whether you’re deadlifting in the garage or doing Olympic lifts on a platform.

For those looking for a complete set, with color coding for different weights, Titan also offers four additional plates—10 lb (grey), 25 lb (green), 35 lb (yellow), and 45 lb (blue)—and for the cost of $518, you can get everything you need to get started. We recommend starting with four to six plates to get your home gym rolling, then adding more as needed.

For lifters who want solid performance without premium pricing, these Titan Fitness plates offer great value on the market.

Adjustable dumbbells save space, but nothing beats the feel of individual iron in your hands. Fixed dumbbells are sturdier, more durable, and have fully knurled chrome handles for a secure, grippy feel—especially when sweating through a tough set. They’re also better suited for circuit-style training, since you don’t need to adjust weights between exercises.

REP Fitness’s Hex Dumbbell Set delivers commercial-gym quality for your home. You can choose from three weight ranges (5-50 lbs, 5-75 lbs, or 5-100 lbs) and pair them with a sleek rack in black, red, or blue. We especially love the chrome handles: They’re knurled end to end for a grippy, no-slip feel that feels premium.

That said, a complete dumbbell set takes up space. Lots of space. The 100-pound set weighs more than 2,000 pounds and spans about six feet of horizontal real estate. It's also not cheap. But if you want the real gym experience at home, these dumbbells are built to outlast your training career.

This adjustable kettlebell from Titan Fitness is “best for beginners” because it nails the fundamentals: It’s reasonably priced (around $150), adjusts from 10 to 40 pounds in seconds, and takes up the same amount of space as a pair of shoes. The weight range covers most beginner-friendly kettlebell movements—from presses and rows to goblet squats, curls, and even cleans and snatches.

If you’re a casual lifter looking to mix in the occasional kettlebell finisher, this one will serve you well. That said, more experienced users will quickly bump against the 40-pound ceiling, especially for swings and deadlifts. And while the plastic housing is sturdy, it doesn’t match the longevity or feel of solid cast iron.

Still, for anyone just getting into kettlebell training, this is the best entry-level option on the market—and a smart way to add variety without cluttering your gym.

Read More: The 6 Best Adjustable Kettlebells

Austin-based Kettlebell Kings has become a small powerhouse in the world of home gym equipment—and these powder-coated models are no exception. Made from single-cast iron with a smooth-yet-grippy powder coat finish, these kettlebells are built to withstand endless swings, snatches, and cleans. The 18 available weight options (ranging from 9 to 106 pounds) make it easy to scale up over time, and the color-coded bands around the handles let you identify weights at a glance.

That quality comes at a cost. Kettlebell Kings’ kettlebells sit at the higher end of the price range—expect to pay around $500 for a full set. But if you want top-tier, American-made bells that’ll last forever, start here. "Whether I’m repping through a set of swings or snatches, I know I can depend on the durable, powder-coated weights," says MH Senior Fitness Editor Brett Williams, NASM.

Metal kettlebells are pricey. And they’re not exactly gentle on your wrists or floors. GoRuck’s Sand Kettlebell is a soft-sided alternative built for tough workouts and easy transport. Shaped like a traditional kettlebell, this canvas training tool can be filled with sand (not included), emptied when not in use, and folded up for on-the-go sessions.

It’s rugged as hell. The double-seal filling system keeps sand from leaking mid-workout. The padded handles add comfort, and GoRuck uses double-pass stitching and a reinforced base to keep the bag from falling apart, even after years of swings, presses, throws, and drops.

Just know this isn’t a direct substitute for a cast-iron bell. If you’re training for kettlebell sport or focusing on technique-heavy movements like snatches or Turkish get-ups, this won’t replicate the same feel. But for general strength and conditioning, it’s a versatile, joint-friendly, and durable option at a fraction of the price.

Plyo box workouts are a great way to build explosive strength, but not at the expense of your shins. REP’s soft plyo boxes feature a wood core and a high-density foam exterior wrapped in grippy vinyl, offering a good balance of structure and comfort.

They come in three heights—16, 20, and 24 inches—and arrive fully assembled. The soft covering helps muffle noise and reduces injury risk if you miss a rep. And while they’re relatively lightweight, each box can handle up to 400 pounds, making them suitable for bigger athletes or weighted jump work.

One thing to note: These boxes aren’t ideal on slick surfaces like tile, polished wood, or smooth concrete. They need some grip to stay put during explosive movements (we’ve made this mistake before). Also, the narrow footprint may feel less stable during lateral movements or box step-overs.

Still, for most home gym users, the REP Plyo Boxes offer a safer, quieter, and more versatile upgrade over the typical wooden box.

Read More: The 7 Best Plyo Boxes According to Certified Trainers

The Hydrow Wave earned a spot on our 2025 Men's Health Home Gym Awards. It pairs a sleek, compact design with surprisingly tranquil, waterway-inspired workouts. Unlike traditional rowers that use noisy air resistance (looking at you, Concept2), the Hydrow Wave uses magnetic resistance for a whisper-quiet ride that won’t disturb the rest of the house.

Yes, it’s pricey. And yes, you’ll need a monthly subscription. But Hydrow’s instructor-led, on-the-water sessions are so vivid and immersive that even longer workouts fly by. Samuel said it feels like you’re actually on the water, and his workouts rarely felt boring on this rower. When your workout is over, just fold it up and store it vertically to save space.

Our only gripe? You can’t skip the scenic classes and program your own intervals. Still, for most users, the guided experience is the main appeal. And when you’re done, the Wave folds upright for easy storage.

The Concept2 RowErg is the standard by which all rowing machines are measured, a device that can redline your heart rate in minutes and is perfect for strengthening hips, glutes, back, and core.

The RowErg with Standard Legs is the new name for Concept2's RowErg rower, and it's the first device that comes to mind when we think of training on a rower at home. Our editors have never been on a better rower than this one, point blank. In a nutshell, it offers many of the same features as the best rowing machines that cost twice as much.

"It's an industry standard used by CrossFit and in many high-profile competitions for a reason," Samuel says. "It relies on a variable resistance flywheel that provides a constant challenge, making it great for high volume or experienced rowers."

It's also extremely easy to assemble (you can see a video of us assembling it here). In our experience (and many Amazon reviewers agree), setup takes around 20 minutes with minimal tools or hardware (just eight screws are required). City dwellers and space-conscious users will appreciate the clever design that lets this machine separate into two pieces for easy storage. Built-in caster wheels make setup and put-away a breeze. Plus, it's surprisingly affordable. This is the definitive home rowing experience.

You can spend $25, $70, even $150 on a jump rope. But you don’t have to. After testing dozens, Men’s Health editors agree: The $6 BOOMIBOO Skipping Rope offers the best bang for your buck. It’s lightweight, durable, and surprisingly smooth thanks to ball-bearing rotation in the handles.

I’ve used this rope regularly for over a year, and it’s held up better than expected. The bearings spin clean, and the foam handles are easy on the hands. My only issue with it is that the length feels a bit off out of the package. You can adjust it (it comes at 9 feet), but I never bothered. I just widened my arms, and it still did the job.

Unless you’re chasing double-unders or elite-level speed, this rope is more than enough—and the price is tough to beat.

Read More: Best Jumping Ropes, Tested By Us

This adjustable weighted jump rope is made of thick silicone that is soft, sweat-resistant, and comfortable for long workouts. Our testing confirms this jump rope is built to last. Out of the box, it's nearly 10 feet long, but is designed to be cut to achieve the perfect fit based on user height. This is ideal for a single user, but doesn't lend itself well to multiple users within the same household unless they're the same height.

Together, the rope and handles weigh 1 pound, so this kit is enough to challenge you during a good cardio sesh. At around $20, this is another great budget-friendly option for anyone looking to get in some cardio at home without a huge piece of equipment.

When you're looking for an exercise bike that's as high-tech as it gets, the Peloton Bike is still our go-to choice. The 22-inch HD touchscreen display is crisp and easy to use, and its library of best-in-class instructor-led studio-style classes is a true game-changer for home workouts. Our editors have used this bike for more than four years now, and have never run out of fresh classes to try.

For nearly $1500, it's a bummer that users need to shell out an additional $24/month for full access to the platform. But for the many Peloton users who have found community in their classes and on the leaderboard, the cost is more than worth it.

Read More: The Best Exercise Bikes, Tested by Us

Manual treadmills may look intimidating, but they have surged in popularity for good reason: They make you work harder, respond instantly to your pace, and run quieter than motorized options. The REP Fitness Strive Treadmill is a standout in the category; it’s a durable curved treadmill that honors its promise as a manuel treadmill and adds a sled push to the equation.

At over 418 pounds, we suggest building this treadmill where you want it and avoid moving it up and down stairs. Still, built-in front wheels let you reposition it if needed. The 400-pound weight capacity makes it a solid pick for larger users, and REP Fitness backs its promise with a 5-year frame warranty—essentially guaranteeing long-term durability.

Yes, it’s big. Yes, it costs almost $4,000. But for runners or serious home gym owners looking for a low-maintenance, high-performance machine, the Strive Treadmill is a wise investment.

NordicTrack is a giant in the treadmill game, and the T10 hits the sweet spot for home gym owners. It’s more compact than the brand’s Commercial 1750, yet still boasts a full-size 60-inch running belt—long enough for sprinting and tall runners alike. Plus, it folds up for easier storage between workouts.

Despite its smaller footprint, the T10 packs in features. You can run up to 12 mph (a 5:00-mile pace) and incline up to 12%. The 10-inch touchscreen pairs with iFit for trainer-led classes, and the Follow Trainer mode automatically adjusts your incline and speed in real time to match the instructor’s terrain.

SmartAdjust learns your fitness level and tailors your workouts based on how you train, while ActivePulse adjusts intensity based on your heart rate (if paired with a compatible monitor). It’s a smart, sturdy, and space-conscious treadmill that’s ideal for intermediate to advanced runners who want a guided experience at home.

Are you aiming to build muscle like a Greek god or shed those pesky love handles? Different goals call for different equipment. If you're into strength training, focus on getting some quality adjustable dumbbells or a full rack setup. For cardio enthusiasts, a treadmill, stationary bike, or rowing machine will get your heart pumping and your sweat dripping.

Unless you're living in a mansion, your home gym likely won't be as spacious as a commercial one. So choose equipment that fits your available space. If you're tight on space, consider compact options like resistance bands or adjustable dumbbells. They're small but mighty, perfect for those who need to optimize their space.

And quality matters, man! Don't skimp on the good stuff. You want equipment that can handle your beastly workouts without falling apart like a house of cards. Look for trusted brands that have a reputation for durability and longevity. Read reviews, ask around, and do your homework. You don't want wobbly machines or weights that crack under pressure. Go for sturdy materials and solid construction. You'll be glad in the long run.

It may be the spice of life, but contrary to what the market may tell you, the basics let you perform the largest variety of movements. Pass on over-specialized tools that let you do a few unique exercises and nothing more. Dumbbells and kettlebells let you do a mix of explosive and controlled isolation moves and can help you build strength, power, and mobility. Opt for those over stability balls and suspension trainers, which require fancier setups (especially if you're building a living room facility).

Set a budget and stick to it. Home gym equipment comes in a wide range of price points, and it's easy to get carried away. Determine how much you're willing to spend and prioritize your purchases accordingly. Remember, it's better to invest in a few quality pieces than to clutter your space with cheap, flimsy gear that won't stand the test of time.

As the Fitness and Commerce Editor at Men's Health, I test and evaluate the best home gym equipment. I collaborated with our team of fitness editors and certified trainers to identify the best home gym equipment worthy of a recommendation, both new and tried-and-true. We spent months hands-on vetting products from top fitness brands, including cardio machines, weights, connected fitness gear, and more.

In fact, we've tested hundreds of pieces of equipment over the years, from the highest-end, commercial-grade models to budget gear from Amazon. Our extensive testing process involved a comprehensive evaluation of multiple factors, including durability, performance, suitability for different fitness levels, and value, to ensure that we recommend only the best. To gather diverse perspectives, we consulted our MH Advisory Board and Strength in Diversity trainers, who shared valuable feedback on the top home gym equipment based on their expertise and experience.

Here are 35 can't-miss items we would include in our dream home gym, with picks that work for just about every space and training style.

So, you're thinking about setting up your very own home gym. Well, buckle up because it's going to be a game-changer.

Convenience is the name of the game. No more wasting precious time commuting to the gym or waiting for your turn on the bench. With a home gym, you're the boss of your own fitness kingdom. You can squeeze in a workout whenever it suits you, whether it's before the crack of dawn or after a long day at work, or in bite-sized bits between meetings. Plus, no more crowds or sweaty gym rats hogging the equipment. It's just you, your favorite tunes, and some iron to conquer.

Sure, creating a lasting home gym demands an initial investment, but it's a wise long-term savings strategy.

Consider adjustable dumbbells (priced between $400 and $800), a yoga mat (typically $20 to $140), and a cardio machine like a rower or bike (average cost around $2000). While that initial investment may seem steep, keep in mind that the average gym membership in the U.S. is about $55/month, plus initiation and cancellation fees. You'll recoup your investment in less than 5 years.

There's nothing worse than investing in a new piece of home gym equipment, only to find it's a one-trick pony you're bored with after a week. For an at-home setup that will keep you excited to use it, you want gear versatile enough to work in different ways. That way, you can keep your space uncluttered and your budget on-point.

When it comes to the best bang-for-your-buck, value-packed equipment, our answer might annoy you. But all you really need? A pair of reliable adjustable dumbbells, a training program, and a weight bench.

Start out strong with a pair of adjustable dumbbells like the ones from SMRTFT or PowerBlock. Yes, they're pricey, but they pack a ton of versatility in a minimal footprint. Pair it with a weight bench like the one from REP Fitness, or a luxe option like this one from Prime Fitness.

To make the most of your equipment, consider a training app like our very own All/Out Studio, which is packed with thousands of programs and guided workouts to keep you engaged and challenged with whatever gear you're working with.

Top it off with a non-slip yoga mat like Lululemon's The Reversible (Un) Mat for a sweat-proof surface for floor exercises, and you've got a recipe for success.

Charles Thorp is the Fitness and Reviews Editor at Men’s Health, where he shares the best product recommendations in gym equipment, recovery tools, supplements, and more. When he’s not writing about training programs or gear, he can be seen at the gym or in the wild, putting them to the test.

#5106. The 7 Best Microcurrent Devices of 2026 Tested by Women’s Health Editors

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

We’re living in the golden age of high-tech skincare devices—and as our beauty editor, I couldn’t be happier. Red light therapy devices, including LED face masks, provide excellent anti-aging benefits from the comfort of our couch, while face steamers have replaced my need for pricey spa facials. Laser hair removal devices are becoming more inclusive by offering technology safe enough for deeper complexions. Face massagers also help de-puff skin after a hangover. However, when it comes to lifting saggy skin, microcurrent devices are the ultimate MVP skincare tool deserving of a spot in your beauty arsenal.

Think of them as a sculpting workout for your face without the sweat. “Microcurrent devices use low levels of electrical current to stimulate facial muscles, helping to boost collagen and sculpt and lift the face,” says dermatologist Marisa Garshick, MD. And don’t worry: These aren’t painful. You’ll notice more of a temporary tingling sensation that’ll disappear within minutes of using the device.

While these at-home machines aren’t as powerful as the ones used by professionals, they’re a more cost-effective option for achieving subtle improvements, says dermatologist Bradley Glodny, MD. You’ll just need some patience to find a weekly cadence and intensity level that works for you. (More on that in a bit.) And if you’re getting seasonal in-office microcurrent treatments, these at-home machines help enhance and sustain your professional results over time, says Dr. Garshick.

What was once a closely guarded secret among my fellow beauty editors and plastic surgeons has now become increasingly popular and readily accessible across our most trusted sites, such as Sephora, Ulta, and Amazon. But an influx of hundreds of options can be overwhelming, which is where I come in. My years of reporting and research have informed this shopping guide. I also consulted the pros about what to look out for when buying at-home microcurrent machines. Ahead are a few non-negotiables to keep in mind, which helped inform the devices we tested and ultimately featured in this story.

Most devices on this list have a range of microcurrent levels—some, like Foreo, even go up to 10. The higher you go, the more intense the microcurrent will feel. If you're accustomed to microcurrent and prefer a device with more power and customization options, opt for one that offers multiple microcurrent levels.

On the other hand, if you're a beginner, you might only need to purchase a device with a few microcurrent levels, such as the NuFace Trinity.

Dr. Garshick advises using your microcurrent device at least three times a week for four to six weeks before you can expect to see results, although some devices recommend daily use. “While much of the initial benefit may only be noticed for hours to days, with consistent use, the results will continue as collagen production can take six or more months,” she says.

After the initial treatment period, you can decrease the frequency of treatments to two to three times per week to maintain your results. Always refer to the specific instructions for use of your microcurrent device.

Many microcurrent devices come with additional features, such as interchangeable attachments, smartphone app connectivity, and even instructional guides.

An added bonus for your microcurrent device is FDA approval, which means that the government organization has determined that the device is safe and effective for its intended use. This is not a necessity when purchasing a microcurrent device, but it's definitely a solid addition if you're looking for something that has been rigorously tested.

You’ll also want to order a microcurrent device that either includes a priming gel or purchase one separately. They’re conductive and allow the electrical currents to be transmitted from the device to the skin. They also help the device glide easily across the skin and help prevent irritation.

Unlike bulky in-office machines, at-home microcurrent devices are about the size of a closed fist. Someone who travels often might prefer the Solawave Facial Wand, a slim option that resembles a T-shaped salad fork. Regardless of which of these featured options you order, they won’t take up too much space in your medicine cabinet or cosmetic bag.

At-home microcurrent machines aren’t exactly cheap. Entry-level models cost around $150, while high-end options can easily go for upwards of $500. However, you’ll save money over time because you get multiple uses out of a single device. And if it helps ease the burden, I spent $275 for a pro microcurrent facial, which costs $60 more than the WH Skincare Award-winning Laduora Lumeo and conductive gel.

With the above dermatological guidance in mind, I began whittling down our list of contenders. The Women’s Health beauty closet was my first stop, along with my at-home collection of skincare devices. Of course, because I’m inquisitive and love knowing what the pros actually use IRL and recommend to their patients, I asked both Dr. Garshick and Dr. Glodny for their fail-safe picks. Next, I tapped our team of skin-obsessive editors and writers, including Brian Underwood, Lily Wohlner, Maridel Reyes, and Cristina Montemayor. And because we prefer only spotlighting products we actually tested, we put them all through a vetting process, which includes:

I eliminated anything that was cumbersome. For example, anything with a short cord or an extra-long one that easily tangled was cut. Were the cordless devices easy to charge quickly if I was in a crunch? Were there any other buttons or features that are easy to accidentally hit while rolling the device across my face?

These aren’t exactly short treatments. We’ll need at least a few minutes per treatment session, so caring for an entire face can easily take 15 minutes or more. I prioritized lightweight, but durable devices that easily slide across my skin. Anything that made my wrist tired after a few minutes was docked points. Was the tingling too intense for beginners or best suited for novices? Are there enough levels for both beginners and experienced users?

This was particularly important because everyone wants a lifted appearance. I evaluated if I noticed any improvements after the first usage, and kept checking in over the last six months. How do the results improve over time?

This was determined based on how each device scores in relation to the above factors. Plus, I asked myself and our team if these are products they’d be willing to repurchase or gift to loved ones because they stand behind the quality of the devices. Ultimately, each of these featured picks met those requirements; here are the results of our labor.

This NuFace device ticks all the boxes on my microcurrent wish list. The lifting effect smoothens the appearance of wrinkles and contours my cheekbones and jawline, even without makeup. The Trinity+ Starter Kit includes accessories to enhance my routine, such as a conductive gel that helps the NuFace glide smoothly across my skin. The device also comes with a lip and eye attachment, allowing me to target smaller problem areas, such as the 11 lines between the brows and smile lines.

This palm-sized powerhouse fits comfortably in my hands, and the five-minute treatment time was quick and easy. It doesn’t sting, and the tingling is mild as long as I use enough conductive gel. The Trinity also beeps, indicating when to move on to a new area of my face. I noticed results after just a few uses, which continued to improve after several months of consistent treatments.

Dr. Glodny and Dr. Garshick also both recommend this device. "This microcurrent device is FDA-cleared, helps to tone facial muscles, and improves the overall contour and appearance of the skin," says Dr. Garshick, adding that it can help rejuvenate the skin and improve skin laxity and the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles.

Honestly, the worst thing I can say about this is the upfront cost. However, I’ve had my device since 2020, and it still performs well six years later. For that reason alone, the NuFace is a long-term investment that delivers fast results that continue to improve over time.

Read more: Best Moisturizers for Mature Skin

When you have a tighter budget, look no further than the sub-$170 Solawave device, which has microcurrent, red light therapy, a facial massage setting, and therapeutic warmth. These settings are great for anti-aging and skin tightening, as well as reducing the look of hyperpigmentation and blemishes. No wonder Dr. Garshick considers it an epic pick for stimulating the muscles, reducing puffiness, improving the appearance of acne, boosting collagen, and enhancing the penetration of other skincare products.

Given its capabilities, the Solawave is comparable to devices that cost twice as much, including the TheraFace Pro. While not as powerful as TheraFace, the Solawave is half the cost, making it an unbeatable tool at an entry-level price point. Purchasing the Solawave is also a power move, as you won’t need to purchase four devices to achieve similar results. Genius!

It’s also gone viral on social media and even earned snaps from the makeup artist for Vanessa Hudgens and the groomer for Pedro Pascal. Most importantly, it left a lasting impression on our team. I like using it in the morning when I want to depuff my face. Whenever I use this device, my skin feels firmer and looks dewy, especially when paired with the Solawave face serum. Together, the microcurrent and red light therapy have been especially helpful for smoothing my skin—it’s like a wrinkle-smoothing iron for my face.

The only downside about this rechargeable device is that it’s less powerful than other microcurrent devices. It only features one preset setting, but with consistent use, you’ll notice long-term improvements. However, if you’re a beginner, then you’ll appreciate the mild tingling.

Yes, this is the priciest option, but the capabilities are next-level great. This is, by far, the smartest microcurrent machine on this list. The Bluetooth-capable device has a smartphone app that allows you to choose from seven different facials, all ranging from four to 14 minutes long. Some focus on sculpting, while others zap acne, brighten your complexion, or smooth out fine lines. To unlock all available treatments, simply sync your device with the app.

Setting up the account on iOS or Android is straightforward, and it includes FAQ tutorials that guide you on how to use the device correctly. Each step of the Ziip device is broken down into easy-to-follow clips that remind you when to move on to a new section of the face for anti-aging benefits. One of my favorite treatments is called “Energize,” which starts at my neck and works its way up to my forehead in about 12 minutes.

It is also unique because Ziip combines microcurrent and nanocurrent technologies. Microcurrent amplifies the lifting effect of jowls and stimulates collagen and elastin for major anti-aging benefits. Meanwhile nanocurrent is a low-intensity, sensitive skin-friendly way to reduce fine lines and enhance skin radiance.

Reyes also adores her ZIIP. "I used it every night, and after a few days, my husband noticed that my face looked more contoured," says Reyes. "The day after I use it, my skin looks smoother and glowier." She relies on it right before important events for more chiseled cheekbones, a sharper jaw, and a slightly lifted brow because it provides instant gratification and is "way less spendy than getting a microcurrent facial at a spa."

I’ve been using the Laduora Lumeo device since it was first released in 2025—and I’ve adored it so much over the past year that I named it the best new microcurrent tool in our 2026 Beauty Awards

So what makes it so worthy of a spot in your routine? For starters, it’s compact. It tucks nicely into my tightly edited cosmetic pouch and carry-on bag without adding extra bulk. TBH, it’s so effective and seamless to use that I’ve ditched my other bulky microcurrent devices and LED face masks in favor of this 4-in-1 device.

Microcurrent gently lifts and defines my cheekbones, while electroporation helps my face serum and cream penetrate more effectively. It also taps into red LEDs to soften my fine lines and wrinkles, while near-infrared light penetrates beneath my skin's surface, helping it feel firmer. Instead of splurging on multiple devices, I can easily get away with just using this single tool.

The best part? Zero downtime! I can rely on this travel-friendly device before special events without irritation, such as redness. Hello, wedding season prep. No wonder the celebrity makeup artists to Jenna Ortega and Naomi Watts rely on it to primp their clients before red carpet events. Need another reason to invest in this tool? It’s a kit that includes the conductive gel, so there’s no need to make a separate purchase. I have oily, acne-prone skin, and it has never caused breakouts.

TBH, it’s hard to pick a downside with this tool. However, if I had to nitpick, I’d like to see it in different colorways, like with the brand’s new microcurrent wands. Still, the functionality is on point, and it costs less than other devices on this list, including the TheraFace. And for that, Laduora will have a permanent spot in my beauty stash.

When you’re short on time, you’ll want to reach for this top-rated Foreo tool. A treatment with this device takes only two minutes, although you can follow up with additional sessions to target specific areas of the face. I like to concentrate on my cheekbones for an extra lift. It’s great for travel, and I found myself using this device more regularly than other devices because the treatments are so quick. The Bear doesn’t feel like a chore, and it's something I can easily use during commercial breaks on TV or while on the phone.

Both Dr. Garshick and Dr. Glodny recommend this cute palm-sized device, which firms and tones skin with microcurrent and massaging T-sonic pulsations that help with sagging skin, reduce puffiness, smooths wrinkles, and relaxes muscles. It's also an FDA-cleared device that boasts a proprietary anti-shock system that ensures you have a safe experience without compromising on results, says Dr. Garshick.

It even helps to relax tension in the face while promoting blood flow. After a few weeks of regular use, my face felt tighter and my eye areas looked more lifted and awake. Not only did my skin look better, but using this device also helped with relieving tension headaches. A single charge can provide 90 uses, so I can take it on the go to these Travel Award-winning destinations even if I forget to pack my charger.

The only downside? The tingling is still noticeable, even with the use of plenty of conductive gel, which means it’s working, but can also be a little uneasy. However, each treatment is only two minutes, so it’s not a deeply uncomfortable experience.

When I saw that this device offers eight treatments in one, I was initially skeptical that the microcurrent attachment wouldn’t be up to par with some of the other devices I tried. I was pleasantly surprised by how effective it was; I saw a difference after using the microcurrent for just a few minutes. But what really sold me was the combination of a powerful microcurrent skin toning device to lift the jowls, along with several magnetic attachments that amplify my skincare routine.

You’ve also got red light therapy and infrared lights to address wrinkles and fine lines, while blue LED light targets acne-causing bacteria. It can also be used as a percussive face massager and comes with multiple brush heads to gently cleanse your face. You can even purchase extra attachments to add a hot and cold ring if needed, which we highly recommend. Warmth provides a spa-like therapeutic vibe, while an icy temperature helps depuff the skin, much like after a raucous night out.This device is a favorite of Dr. Glodny, and Wohlner has been using it for a few months. She’s a big fan of the various skin benefits, especially the trifecta of microcurrent, LED therapy, and cryotherapy. "It seems intimidating if you’re a beginner, but this tool truly makes my life so much easier for banishing acne, tightening my skin, and waking me up when I didn’t get enough sleep the night before,” says Wohlner.

Pesky adult acne and redness have been cosmetic concerns for Wohlner, but the TheraFace Pro has helped solve her skincare woes. She saw some initial glowy finish, but achieved the most visible anti-aging results after a few weeks of regular use.

While some microcurrent devices also relieve jaw tension, when using the percussion attachments in conjunction with the microcurrent, Wohlner found that her jaw muscles felt more relaxed and looked more toned than ever. The combination of those treatments in this single device truly sets it apart in terms of effectiveness. “I also struggle with jaw pain from grinding my teeth, and the percussive therapy this device offers is a major game-changer when I wake up with a sore jaw," says Wohlner.

You can’t go wrong with this tool, but if you won’t realistically incorporate at least a few of these modalities into your routine, it’s probably best to save some money and stick with a more affordable alternative. That said, we’re big fans and have gifted some to our lucky loved ones, including our moms, who are fine-tuning their mature skincare routines.

NYC eyebrow guru Joey Healy created the ultimate microcurrent for lifting the delicate skin around your eye area. It's not uncommon for your brows to start sagging with age, making your eyes appear droopier and more closed off. If you have hooded eyes, this effect is even more pronounced. This microcurrent device is made specifically to target the eyebrow area and tighten the skin around the browbone, giving hooded eyes a lifted, more awake appearance.

Montemayor gave this device a solid five stars because she noticed a noticeable difference in her eyebrows after using it. Even after her first go, her droopy eyebrow was even with her other one. She tells us that this device is super powerful; she can't even fathom using the highest level. Another reason to love this device? It automatically powers down after 15 minutes of use, preventing skin overstimulation and accidental battery drain.

The only downside of this device is that it uses batteries. While we wish it were rechargeable, this device is cordless, which is particularly helpful for anyone with limited outlets in their home.

Microcurrent devices aren't exactly cheap—the most affordable ones are still over $100, though the best ones tend to be around $300. Just be sure to use your device consistently at least three times a week, as Dr. Garshick mentioned.

If you're hesitant, she recommends chatting with your dermatologist about your skincare concerns and goals. They can help you come up with a treatment plan to supplement the use of your microcurrent device, optimizing the benefits of it.

Additional reporting by Addison Aloian, NASM-CPT and Cristina Montemayor.

#5105. White House sends crypto-relevant picks to fill SEC and CFTC seats

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

Of the nominees, Nathan Anonick and Matthew Rowland have worked on the Clarity Act, while Kristin Johnson has regularly spoken about digital asset regulations.

The White House nominated four individuals to fill vacant seats at the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, making the first such nominations in roughly a year.

Nathan Anonick of Virginia and Matthew Rowland of the District of Columbia were nominated to be commissioners of the CFTC. Kristin N. Johnson of Michigan and Steven Levine of Maryland were nominated to be members of the SEC.

The nominations are bipartisan — Anonick and Levine are Republicans; Johnson and Rowland are Democrats. The Senate Agriculture Committee will consider the CFTC nominees, while the Senate Banking Committee will consider the SEC nominees.

Anonick currently serves as legislative counsel to Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman John Boozman and worked as a lead negotiator on the Agriculture Committee's portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. Rowland is a CFTC attorney who has been detailed to the Senate Agriculture Committee and also worked on the Clarity Act and the 2024 Agriculture Committee crypto bill.

Meanwhile, Johnson, a former CFTC commissioner, focused on digital assets, risk management, and market integrity. Johnson has spoken often about crypto and the need for regulations around crypto asset custody, DeFi, and AI.

Levine most recently served as General Counsel and a senior advisor at the White House Council of Economic Advisers, and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda.

Levine was nominated to succeed Hester Peirce, a vocal advocate for the crypto industry who led the agency's Crypto Task Force and assisted Chairman Paul Atkins' Project Crypto to modernize securities regulation to accommodate crypto innovation and advance the goal of making the U.S. the "crypto capital of the world."

Ji Kim, chief executive of the Crypto Council for Innovation, congratulated the nominees in a post on X, stating that strong, bipartisan representation is essential to developing durable rules that safeguard markets, protect consumers, and support innovation.

"Both the CFTC and SEC will continue to play central and consequential roles in our financial markets, and together these nominees bring a wealth of experience and expertise that will help ensure continued American leadership," Kim wrote.

#5104. The 10 Best Face Washes for Men in 2026, Tested by Grooming Editors

Soaps from Kiehl’s and Tower 28 came out on top in our testing.

Our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

EVERY GOOD SKINCARE routine starts with the same thing—a quality face wash. Before you layer on serums, moisturizers, and eye creams, you need to clear the canvas. A face wash does exactly that by clearing away dirt and grime that accumulate on your skin while also helping prevent clogged pores that can trigger breakouts. That’s why it’s crucial to find the best face wash for you, no matter your skin type.

Wash your face every morning, night, and after heavy workouts to remove bacteria and sebum before they build up, says dermatologistDr. Anthony Rossi, MD. The best face washes for men go beyond cleaning: they hydrate, fight acne, and control excess oil. This first step in your routine is especially important if you live an active lifestyle. While cardio workouts boost circulation and support collagen production, sweat can leave your skin vulnerable to breakouts and irritation.

With so many products out there, finding the right one for your skin type and preferences can feel impossible. That’s why I spent the last two years testing every cleanser I could get my hands on to find the ten best face washes for virtually any skin type and price point.

A face wash is the cornerstone of any skincare routine—without it, the rest of your products won’t work as well. Choose one that’s gentle yet effective because even if your entire routine is just washing your face, you don’t want a cleanser that strips away your skin’s natural oils.

Matching your face wash to your skin type ensures it works with your skin’s natural needs, clears and balances your complexion, and primes your face for the products that follow.

We’ve been testing face washes and cleansers since this story was first published in 2021. As Men's Health's Grooming Editor, I’m also constantly trying out the latest releases to determine which are worth adding to your rotation. For this update, I considered picks from previous iterations of this roundup, as well as current favorites from fellow Men's Health writers and editors. This ultimately led to me testing over 50 face washes, evaluating their ingredients, feel, consistency, and effectiveness. Below is the culmination of this extensive hands-on research: the ten best face washes for men with any skin type or budget.

For active guys who want a no-nonsense soap that still feels luxurious, this cleanser from Kiehl's delivers. Formulated with hydrating glycerin and squalane—and free of parabens and fragrances—it thoroughly cleanses without stripping moisture. Its powerful ingredients clean and hydrate at the same time, leaving your skin soft, balanced, and primed for the rest of your routine.

Testing Notes: I’ve used Kiehl's cleanser for years and love its ultra-smooth formula that glides easily over my skin. I appreciate that it’s fragrance-free, making it ideal for sensitive skin. Lightweight, gentle, moisturizing, and nourishing, it’s one of the most versatile cleansers I’ve tried—perfect for any skin type. At $16 for 2.5 oz, it isn’t the cheapest option, but it’s still on the affordable side of the market. Because it foams so well, I only need a small amount for a full wash, and one container lasts me about two months with daily use. Overall, Kiehl's Ultra Facial Cleanser remains my go-to everyday face wash, no matter your skin type or budget.

This gel cleanser uses zinc, copper, and magnesium to support the skin’s natural defenses while boosting hydration. Aloe vera then locks in moisture and forms a soothing barrier, while oat calms irritation and comforts sensitive skin. Fragrance-free, it gently removes makeup, sunscreen, and daily buildup without stripping or irritating—even for the most reactive skin.

Testing Notes: I don’t have rosacea, but my skin is prone to redness, so I was excited to see this cleanser approved by the National Rosacea Society—and it didn’t disappoint. Whenever my skin flares up, I use it daily, and within a week or two (depending on severity), the redness quickly calms. Its silky consistency also leaves my skin feeling smooth, balanced, and healthy.

You can’t go wrong with a classic. This Cetaphil cleanser, formulated for combination to oily, sensitive skin, actively removes dirt and excess oil while protecting your skin’s natural barrier. The blend of B vitamins and glycerin nourishes as it cleanses, leaving your face refreshed, balanced, and never tight or dry.

Testing Notes: Cetaphil’s Daily Facial Cleanser delivers incredible value for its price. I love that it packs the same hero ingredients you’d see in pricier formulas, like glycerin and niacinamide, yet it’s gentle enough for even ultra-sensitive skin. It leaves my face feeling clean but never stripped, which makes it easy to reach for every day. My only gripe? I wish the pump dispenser worked more smoothly—it can be frustrating when I’m half-asleep and just want a quick wash.

Long before CeraVe went viral on TikTok, grooming experts swore by the drugstore brand for its high-quality ingredients at budget-friendly prices. A perfect example is this cleanser, packed with hydrating staples like hyaluronic acid and ceramides that strengthen the skin barrier while keeping moisture locked in.

Testing Notes: CeraVe’s Facial Cleanser is one of my go-to budget face washes because it’s easy to find online or in stores, and it simply works. I’ve been using CeraVe since my early 20s, and I can honestly say the formula has never let me down—it removes excess oil and grime without ever causing breakouts.

Shaped like a deodorant stick but designed for your face, this solid soap from Oars and Alps packs charcoal, a buzzy exfoliant that gently scrubs without irritation. I love that even a 1.4-oz container lasts over a month when used daily.

Testing Notes: Oars and Alps’ cleansing stick has become my go-to TSA-friendly face soap for traveling and camping. I love how portable it is and how easily it applies—just like my favorite deodorant—while still exfoliating and removing dirt. It easily fits in my Dopp kit, and I don’t need to worry about it leaking or opening. Plus, my face feels incredibly clean after each use, and a little product really does go a long way.

Finding a TSA-friendly cleanser that doesn't spill is hard. That's where Jaxon Lane's Shake and Wake comes in. It's a powder-to-cream product that gently exfoliates skin and cleans just as well as a liquid cleanser, thanks to a powerful combo of niacinamide, vitamin E, and vitamin C. In other words, it's a Dopp kit must-have.

Testing Notes: The first thing I noticed about this wash was its powdery consistency. What surprised me was how much I liked it—and how often I keep reaching for it, especially when traveling. Similar to Oars and Alps Solid Wash, there is minimal risk of spilling—and even if it did (which I’ve yet to experience), the powder will be far less destructive than liquid.

It feels ultra-gentle on my skin and transforms into a soap-like lather as soon as it hits water. The container is TSA-friendly, tightly sealed, and unlikely to leak, and since it’s powder, even a spill would be minimal and far less messy than a gel.

If you're somebody who loves the smell of the great outdoors, or that irreplaceable feeling felt (and smelt) the early morning after a night of camping, then this face wash is for you. Loaded with skin-boosting natural ingredients like aloe vera, caffeine, and charcoal, Dr. Squatch's face wash exfoliates, refreshes, and cleanses with the best of them.

Testing Notes: With its unique charcoal-backed texture and feel, this wash is one of the most rejuvenating options out there. But what really stands out is its understated, yet still attention-grabbing pine tar scent—subtle enough to avoid clashing with your cologne, but woodsy enough to raise the nostrils in the best way possible.

For those with sensitive or dry skin, there are few (if any) better skincare brands than La Roche-Posay. And the brand's cleanser is a perfect representation of why. Its niacinamide-backed formula is equally gentle and hydrating. Add in other moisturizing winners like glycerin, along with the lack of any skin-aggravating ingredients like heavy fragrances or sulfates, and you have one of the lowest risk, highest reward face washes on the market.

Testing Notes: I have sensitive skin and love this cleanser because it never irritates me. Even if your skin is less reactive, the creamy lather feels amazing during and after each wash. It’s gentle and leaves skin feeling hydrated and healthy.

Talk about value—at under $7 a container, it’s hard to find a more effective, affordable face wash for men than Harry’s. Best known for its stellar shave gear, the brand has quietly expanded into no-nonsense men’s skincare, including standouts like its facial moisturizer. This face wash follows the same formula: it packs low-key hydrators like eucalyptus and peppermint alongside gentle exfoliants like glycerin, delivering a no-BS cleanse that gets the job done without breaking the bank.

Testing Notes: Harry’s hasn’t strayed from its facial-hair roots, as this cleanser doubles as one of the best beard washes, softening whiskers and priming them for trimming or shaving. I also can’t overstate how foamy it gets; it not only strips away dirt and buildup but also makes each (already affordable) container last a long time.

Anyone who struggles with acne knows it takes over your routine, demanding protective, non-invasive, blemish-correcting products at every step. For that crucial first cleanse, Geologie’s new Acne Control Face Wash stands out as the best option. Even though it’s been on the market for barely a year, it has already become a staple for me whenever I’m facing a breakout, thanks to its 2 percent salicylic acid formula and silky-smooth application.

Testing Notes: I still reach for this wash whenever I feel a blemish or breakout coming on. The only drawback is that the gel feels a little stringy at first and needs plenty of water before it foams. Once it does, though, the lather expands quickly, and a dime-sized drop covers my entire face—making each bottle last for months.

Wash your face twice a day—morning and night. Just as important, pay attention to the products you use, avoiding harsh chemicals like sulfates and parabens. Choose a gentle cleanser for everyday use and keep an exfoliating scrub for two or three times a week. Apply the scrub with light pressure—fast, hard, and rough isn’t the answer. Overdoing it can damage your skin and create new problems. And always remember: everyone’s skin type is different. What works for one person might not work for another.

#5103. What Are Solana Privacy Rings? Inside Helius’ Privacy Protocol for Solana

Every transaction on Solana is public by default. Anyone can look up a wallet address and see its balance, what it has sent and received, and when. That transparency is useful for verifying the network, but a problem for anyone who doesn't want their finances on display: a business paying salaries, a trader building a position, or an individual who simply doesn't want strangers seeing their savings.

Rings are programmable, onchain environments for encrypting money, markets, and finance - without ever leaving Solana

Now live on mainnet. pic.twitter.com/ezCIUCjcbI

Rings support SOL and other tokens on Solana, including SPL and Token-2022 tokens. Users keep custody of their funds throughout, since every transaction needs the owner's signature.

Crucially, the private balances live on the same network as everything else. Private transactions execute directly on Solana and encrypted data is stored on Solana's ledger, with no separate layer-2 network or sequencer in between. That means private balances sit alongside the same stablecoins, tokenized assets and DeFi liquidity as public ones.

Each private transfer comes with a zero-knowledge proof, a piece of cryptography that lets the network confirm the transfer is valid, for example that the sender actually had the funds, without revealing the numbers involved. Rings use a type of zero-knowledge proof called a Groth16 zk-SNARK, which Helius says can be generated in tens of milliseconds, either by a service provider or on the user's own device. Each private transfer settles in a single Solana transaction.

Users read their own encrypted balances with a viewing key. They can decrypt their balance locally, or let a service provider decrypt it and serve it to them, and they can share a key for a single transaction with an auditor or counterparty without exposing the rest of their history.

Moving funds into a Ring from an ordinary public wallet, or back out again, is visible onchain, including the asset and amount. But users who on-ramp from fiat currency straight into a private balance, through a supported provider, keep the asset and amount hidden from the start, according to Helius.

Because Custom Rings interoperate with the default Ring, regulated firms can keep their activity confidential from the market while still sharing the same liquidity as everyone else.

Private transfers are just the start. Solana programs can hold encrypted balances in private escrows and release them when set conditions are met, opening the way for:

At launch, Decrypt, mining and staking app ORE and cross-chain service Aurora Intents were using the default Ring, while Backpack, DFlow, Jupiter, Squads and Titan were among the teams working on integrations.

Helius says the core programs and zero-knowledge circuits have been audited by security firms Certora, OtterSec and ZK Security. Engineers from the Solana Foundation, Blueshift, Zcash and other teams took part in the "trusted setup," the one-off ceremony that generates the parameters the proofs rely on.

The code is open source, published on GitHub under the Apache 2.0 license, so anyone can inspect how it works.

Formal verification, a mathematical check that the circuits behave exactly as intended, is still underway and expected to finish by the end of 2026. Solana's own documentation currently describes Rings as being in beta.

#5102. TRM Labs launches new service to help police seize stolen crypto in minutes

Looking for institutional-grade crypto trading? Discover LMAX Digital, the regulated exchange from LMAX Group

TRM Labs has launched Beacon Concierge, a managed service that enables any verified law enforcement agency to work with exchanges and stablecoin issuers to seize illicit crypto funds.

TRM Labs has launched Beacon Concierge, a managed service that enables any verified law enforcement agency to work with exchanges and stablecoin issuers to interdict and seize illicit cryptocurrency funds on any chain in any asset.

According to TRM's Thursday release, the company pointed out that many law enforcement agencies lack direct relationships or the capacity to package requests correctly and act while funds remain in motion. In large incidents, stolen funds have been split across thousands of transactions within days.

The new service is built on the Beacon Network, which TRM Labs launched in August 2025. The network has more than 200 members covering 80% of crypto trading volume. When flagged funds reach a member, the average time to action is measured in minutes, the press release said.

TRM said Beacon Concierge has already supported 15 cases for 14 agencies in 10 countries, with more than $35 million frozen. More than $200 million has been interdicted with Beacon members to date, the company added.

The company's own investigators assist agencies by tracing funds, preparing evidence packages, flagging addresses in the network, and supporting requests for freeze and seizure. Stablecoin issuers can freeze funds on-chain.

"Criminals move quickly, and the agencies pursuing them need a clear path to the issuers who can act," said Esteban Castaño, CEO and co-founder of TRM Labs. "Beacon Concierge puts our investigators, our tracing and the Beacon Network behind every verified agency, so more cases can move from first lead to issuer action."

TRM cited the Beacon Network's response to the Binance exploit as an illustration of the scale involved.

The network has labeled more than 26,000 addresses across 14 blockchains, traced more than 67,000 transfers and links, including over 1,050 cross-chain swaps. TRM said the network followed funds from 59 origin addresses an average of 10 hops and as far as 71.

Network members flagged 39% of the addresses, while Beacon identified the other 61% automatically from those flags. The network delivered more than 45,000 alerts to participating platforms, the company added.

"The Binance hack shows why cross-chain and multi-asset coordination is more important than ever," TRM said. "No investigator could have followed every branch by hand. Beacon Concierge is built so that any agency, not only those with a large team and an existing issuer relationship, can put that kind of coverage behind a case."

An agency can join the network with a single verification process, TRM said. The company will handle tracing, evidence packaging, flagging, and routing, while prioritizing the cases by severity.

Accelerating developments in AI are enabling attackers to launch more sophisticated cyberattacks at scale, especially as they utilize the technology to find vulnerabilities undetected by humans. DefiLlama data shows $8.78 billion has been lost across 341 crypto hacks and exploits year-to-date, led by a $6.36 billion breach at Binance.

#5101. The 10 Best Red Light Therapy Tools of 2026, Tested by Beauty Experts

Our top picks—from Omnilux, TheraFace, and Qure—treat acne, boost collagen, and more.

Women's Health may earn commission from the links on this page, but we only feature products we believe in. Why Trust Us?

If you're starting to notice that your skin is looking a little, well, tired, you're not alone. The visible signs of aging—I’m talking fine lines and wrinkles, dullness, even sallow skin—will strike us all sooner or later. Bummer. On the bright side, we're living in an age when there's no shortage of smart beauty devices and skincare products for these issues. From wrinkle-smoothing injections like Botox and fillers to anti-aging creams, you've got an arsenal of skin-boosting tools at your disposal.

But what if I were to tell you that there's one such solution that takes roughly 10 a day and can be done while you're relaxing in bed scrolling TikTok? Enter red light therapy.

Red light therapy has exploded in popularity lately because it's convenient, noninvasive, and can be done at home. It uses a specific spectrum of visible light that offers a host of beauty benefits—low-level laser light therapy can effectively treat scars, vitiligo, and psoriasis, research shows. It has an anti-inflammatory effect and can even help to smooth wrinkles, too. So, how does it work? We know that red light penetrates 2 to 3 millimeters into skin's dermis, where it's “absorbed by light-sensitive porphyrins in the mitochondria of skin cells, stimulating energy production in fibroblasts to churn out more collagen,” says dermatologist Ava Shamban, MD.

But the goodness doesn't stop there. Red light can also help fade dark spots and manage eczema, plus boost hair growth, says dermatologist Purvisha Patel, MD. These at-home devices can be expensive, but they're an investment you can use for a years to come: Many red light therapy tools are also equipped with blue lights, which are particularly effective at treating acne (say buh-bye to those period or menopausal breakouts) and other concerns. Bottom line: At any age—and for years to come—these red light therapy tools can be a beneficial addition to your beauty routine.

Ultimately, these are the devices that we’ll continue to use and would genuinely repurchase if we had to start our skincare routine from scratch. The best part? Our faves start at just $72, which is a major win for a category that easily ranges from $300 to $700.

I've got a great list of options for you, but if you find yourself in the market for a red light therapy tool, here are a few things to keep in mind.

There are several kinds of red light therapy devices to choose from, including panels, masks, and facial wands, and one may be a better fit for you based on your lifestyle and the area you're seeking to treat.

LED masks are the most common variety you'll find for home use because most are hands-free and contain a lot of diodes (a fancy way of referring to the individual lightbulbs), offering a powerful burst of light to treat the face, neck, or chest.

Maybe you're claustrophobic and the idea of wearing masks gives you the heebie-jeebies—that's where panels come in. They look like flexible bodyboards that you lie down under, and they come in a diverse range of shapes and sizes, each offering different levels of red light exposure to your face, décolletage, and back. These also help replace the need for a separate lip-specific red light therapy tool.

Wands are appealing when you want to target smaller specific areas (the crow's feet or smile lines, for example) and prefer to do your treatments on the go (you can walk around while using these).

Our eyes are the first place to show signs of aging, so you’ll want to take a cue from dermatologist Pooja Rambhia, MD, and use these affordable red light therapy eye tools. Red, deep red, and near-infrared wavelengths target fine lines, wrinkles, darkness, and puffiness early on, making them a smart preventive beauty move.

It's tempting to pick a device with the quickest treatment window, especially if you don't have loads of free time to sit back and chill with a red light mask. But remember: To treat more advanced signs of aging, a longer treatment time may be more beneficial. Look at the full picture before you base your purchase on the convenience of a quicker treatment. And for what it’s worth, almost all of our featured recommendations can be used in just three minutes, so even busy women can incorporate quick treatments into their routine.

You may notice the abbreviation nm on the outer packaging of many of these tools. This stands for nanometers and refers to the wavelength of the light that the device emits—an important metric to consider, says dermatologist Jody A. Levine, MD. "Red light typically falls between 630 and 660 nanometers, and is good for targeting fine lines and mild discoloration," says Dr. Levine. If you're looking for something slightly more powerful—to deal with deeper wrinkles, sagging, or stubborn pigmentary problems—go with a device that cranks up to the near-infrared range (between 800 and 850 nanometers) to penetrate deeper.

Our beauty team is well-versed in red light therapy tools. We’ve been updating this story since December 2022—and I’ve been writing about these devices since November 2019. I've also been using red light therapy tools since April 2018. They've significantly diminished my stubborn fine lines and hyperpigmentation—and when I stop for a few months, they slowly reappear. Consistency is key, so we tested dozens of red light therapy devices for over two years to determine which ones are worth purchasing and can help us maintain wrinkle-free skin.

Since there are quite literally thousands of options available on Amazon alone, I asked dermatologists about their no-fail picks. Next, I recruited WH staffers—beauty director Brian Underwood, associate style & commerce editor Shannen Zitz, and associate health and fitness editor Addison Aloian—and our beauty contributors—Erica Metzger, Lily Wohlner, and Lisa DeSantis—for their suggestions. After compiling a comprehensive list of promising new launches, old standbys, and products that align with derm guidance, we got to testing.

We spent a minimum of three weeks evaluating attributes like ease of use, treatment time, comfort, any tangible results, and overall value. Of the 22 devices tested, these 10 delivered the best results in our in-depth testing process.

Beyond keeping expert guidance in mind—type, nanometers, and time commitment—we considered our long- and short-term results. We also considered each product’s durability over the years, and eliminated anything that doesn’t remain in top shape. Ahem, don’t forget to clean your LED face masks to help with their longevity. We also tried the latest drops and the Women’s Health Beauty Award-winning Solawave Neck & Chest Pro Light Therapy Mask took the crown as our favorite launch of the year. Ultimately, these are the devices that we’ll continue to use and would genuinely repurchase if we had to start our skincare routine from scratch. The best part? Our faves start at just $72, which is a major win for a category that easily ranges from $300 to $700.

Simply put: It’s a fast-acting device that requires a minimal commitment and provides the most anti-aging coverage among all of the featured picks.

Unlike a single-wavelength treatment, CurrentBody Series 2 combines red, near-infrared, and deep near-infrared lights to target multiple concerns in one session. Hyperpigmentation from zits? Faded. #5100. Bitcoin Faces First Back-to-Back Annual Losses in History, But There's a Catch

Bitcoin Faces First Back-to-Back Annual Losses in History, But There's a Catch

Bitcoin is flirting with a historical first that bulls probably don’t want to hear: Two consecutive years of losses, something the cryptocurrency has never experienced in its 18-year history.

The world's largest cryptocurrency finished 2025 down 6.34% and has lost another 15.65% so far in 2026, trading around $73,850 on November 10. If Bitcoin fails to recover above its annual opening price of roughly $87,500 before December 31, it will close two calendar years in the red for the first time.

Historical annual returns show Bitcoin has experienced several brutal crashes since its creation, but each negative calendar year has been followed by a positive one. Even the disastrous 2018 and 2022 bear markets failed to produce consecutive annual losses.

The historical pattern is clear. Its significance, however, deserves a closer look.

Bitcoin's previous annual crashes were considerably more painful than its current losing streak. The cryptocurrency plunged 73.56% in 2018 and another 64.27% in 2022, wiping out most of investors' holdings in each respective year.

By comparison, Bitcoin's 6.34% decline in 2025 was relatively mild. Add the roughly 16% loss recorded this year, and the combined decline comes to approximately 21% after accounting for compounding.

That's a fraction of the losses investors endured in previous crypto winters, despite the market potentially recording a longer sequence of negative annual returns.

Bitcoin's performance in 2024 also provides some perspective. The cryptocurrency surged more than 120% that year, meaning investors who bought at the beginning of 2024 would still be sitting on substantial gains despite the subsequent decline.

The picture changes considerably when measuring losses from the market's actual peak instead of calendar-year boundaries.

Bitcoin reached approximately $126,000 in October 2025 before crashing below $58,000 during 2026. That represented a decline exceeding 50%, a significantly more painful move than the 21% combined loss reflected in the two annual candlesticks.

Analysts have pointed to Bitcoin's increasingly institutional investor base, spot exchange-traded funds, and deeper market liquidity as potential explanations for its comparatively smaller bear-market drawdowns.

Those structural changes may help explain why Bitcoin's current market cycle looks different from previous ones, although they have not eliminated major price crashes.

There is also a distinction between the length of a losing streak and the severity of the losses. A market can decline slowly over several calendar years without inflicting the same damage as a single catastrophic year.

And Bitcoin has already demonstrated that a bad year doesn't necessarily translate into a prolonged downturn. The cryptocurrency gained roughly 92% in 2019 following its 2018 collapse and surged more than 155% in 2023 after its disastrous 2022 performance.

For now, Bitcoin has 50 days left in 2026 to avoid its first back-to-back annual losses. A third consecutive decline in 2027 would extend the streak further, but that scenario is still hypothetical.

At its November 10 price of approximately $73,850, Bitcoin would need to gain about 18.5% to recover its 2026 opening price and finish the year in positive territory.
